## Description

When a cron job runs and the session title auto-generation fails (model unavailable, timeout, API error), the cron session ends up with a **blank title** in the session sidebar/history. This degrades session recall quality and makes it hard to identify sessions.

- Cron scheduler (`cron/scheduler.py`)
- Title generator (`agent/title_generator.py`)

items.title: fix(cron): race condition between title generation and session close in cron jobs

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Description

Cron sessions are never getting auto-generated titles because the cron scheduler's `run_job()` function does not call `auto_title_session()`, unlike the CLI/gateway/TUI/ACP paths which all invoke `maybe_auto_title()` after the first exchange.

This causes a regression where all cron sessions in the personal profile have blank titles, degrading session recall and nightly synthesis quality.

## Expected behavior

Add a synchronous `auto_title_session()` call after successful cron job completion, before the session is closed in the finally block. Using the synchronous call (rather than the daemon-thread `maybe_auto_title()`) guarantees the title is persisted before `_session_db.close()` tears down the connection.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (upstream main)
- Cron scheduler (`cron/scheduler.py`)
- Title generator (`agent/title_generator.py`)

items.body:
## Description

When two sessions would get the same auto-generated title (e.g. both start with "Debugging Python Import Errors"), the call to `set_session_title()` raises a `ValueError` that is silently swallowed. This means the title is never persisted and the session ends up with no title.

## Expected behavior

When a title collision is detected, a unique suffix should be appended (e.g., "Debugging Import Error #2") using `get_next_title_in_lineage()` if the session database supports it. If the session database does not support lineage-based deduplication, the error should propagate.

## Additional hardening

When `set_session_title()` returns `False` (session not found between title generation and storage), a `RuntimeError` should be raised instead of silently failing, so callers can detect the issue.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (upstream main)
- Title generator (`agent/title_generator.py`)

items.title: [Bug]: Kanban plugin uses native browser dialogs instead of in-app ConfirmDialog

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Bug Description

The Hermes Kanban dashboard plugin (`plugins/kanban/dashboard/dist/index.js`) calls native browser dialogs (`window.confirm`, `window.prompt`, `window.alert`) for destructive confirmations and required-input prompts. The host web frontend already has proper in-app dialog primitives (Radix-based `@nous-research/ui`), but they are not exposed on the plugin SDK surface, so the plugin falls back to the browser's OS-styled dialogs.

Concrete symptoms a user sees in Chrome:

- Dragging a task card from "Done" → "Blocked" produces a Chrome confirm dialog: **"Mark this task as blocked? The worker's claim is released."** with default OS-styled buttons.
- Marking a task as done produces a Chrome prompt for the completion summary: a tiny single-line OS-styled input that scrolls horizontally for anything longer than a sentence.
- Submitting an empty completion summary triggers a **second** Chrome alert: "Completion summary is required before marking a task done." — a dialog firing from a dialog, breaking the flow.
- Trashing a task, archiving a board, removing an attachment, and the CLI-hint clipboard fallback all show the same OS-styled chrome. Bulk-many confirmations use singular copy ("Permanently delete this task?") even when 3 tasks are selected.

The host main dashboard already uses `ConfirmDialog`, `Dialog`, and `useToast` from `@nous-research/ui` — these are battle-tested Radix wrappers. The plugin can't use them because `window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__` (`web/src/plugins/registry.ts:104`) does not expose any dialog primitive.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes dashboard --no-open --port 9120` (or any port).
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:9120/kanban` in Chrome.
3. Create or open any task card.
4. Drag the card to a different column (e.g. Ready → Blocked).
5. **Observed:** Chrome shows an OS-styled confirm dialog. Buttons do not match the dashboard's visual language.
6. Right-click the card, choose "Mark Done" (or drag to Done).
7. **Observed:** Chrome shows an OS-styled prompt for the completion summary — single line, ugly.
8. Click OK without typing anything.
9. **Observed:** Chrome shows a SECOND OS-styled alert: "Completion summary is required before marking a task done."
10. Select multiple tasks, drag them to the Trash zone.
11. **Observed:** Chrome confirm says "Permanently delete this task?" (singular) — bulk-many copy is wrong.

## Expected Behavior

In-app dialogs that match the host dashboard's visual language (Radix/shadcn via `@nous-research/ui`), with:

- A multi-line textarea for completion summaries (not single-line).
- Inline validation that disables the confirm button until valid input is provided (no second dialog).
- Pluralized copy for bulk-many operations: "Permanently delete 3 selected tasks?" / "Delete 3 tasks" with an expandable list showing per-task summary fields.
- A single contextual SVG icon next to the title (Check, Archive, Pause, Trash, Paperclip) — one per dialog, not four.
- Auto-focus the textarea on open + scroll into view for mobile keyboards.
- Cancel button stays clickable during the PATCH (only the confirm button shows the spinner) so users can abort slow networks.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter submits the textarea.
- Transient error feedback via the existing `useToast` hook; sticky errors keep the current banner pattern.

A working prototype with all four variants side-by-side is at `docs/design/kanban-dialogs/index.html` on the branch `fix/kanban-native-dialogs` ([link](https://github.com/DavidMetcalfe/hermes-agent/blob/fix/kanban-native-dialogs/docs/design/kanban-dialogs/index.html)). Open it in any browser — no build step. The recommended design is "Variant B-refined" in the prototype.

## Actual Behavior

12 native browser dialogs across 6 flows (see "Root Cause Analysis" for exact file:line). All OS-styled, all inconsistent with the host dashboard. Bulk-many pluralization is missing. Validation triggers a second alert.

## Affected Component

- Other (Kanban dashboard plugin — `plugins/kanban/dashboard/`)

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

Not applicable — this is a frontend plugin issue, no gateway/agent debug logs are relevant. The bug is reproducible on a fresh `hermes update` install with no custom config.

## Operating System

macOS 26.5.1

## Python Version

3.11.15

## Hermes Version

`hermes update` to current (HEAD `abbf8787e` on `main` at time of filing).

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```
$ rg -n 'window\.(alert|confirm|prompt)' plugins/kanban/dashboard/dist/index.js
188:    window.alert(tx(t, "completionSummaryRequired", ...));
179:    const value = window.prompt(...);
678:    if (confirmMsg && !window.confirm(confirmMsg)) return;
714:    if (confirmMsg && !window.confirm(confirmMsg)) return;
852:    if (confirmMsg && !window.confirm(confirmMsg)) return;
943:    if (!window.confirm(tx(t, "trash.confirm", ...))) return ...;
958:    if (!window.confirm(tx(t, "trash.confirmMany", ...))) return ...;
1251:  const fallback = function () { window.prompt("Copy this command:", cmd); };
1831:  if (window.confirm(msg)) props.onDeleteBoard(props.board);
2202: if (window.confirm(tx(t, "trash.confirmMany", ...))) { ... };
2890: if (opts && opts.confirm && !window.confirm(opts.confirm)) { ... };
3168: if (window.confirm(tx(i18n, "confirmRemoveAttachment", ...))) { ... };
```

12 sites, all `window.{alert,confirm,prompt}`.

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The plugin is a single IIFE bundle at `plugins/kanban/dashboard/dist/index.js` (no JSX, no bundler — `dist/` IS the source). It uses `window.__HERMES_PLUGIN_SDK__` for React, hooks, and shadcn primitives — see `web/src/plugins/registry.ts:104-168`. The SDK currently exposes:

- React, hooks, `api`, `fetchJSON`, `authedFetch`, `buildWsUrl`, `buildWsAuthParam`
- `components`: `Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardContent`, `Badge`, `Button`, `Checkbox`, `Input`, `Label`, `Select`, `SelectOption`, `Separator`, `Tabs`, `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger`, `PluginSlot`
- `utils`: `cn`, `timeAgo`, `isoTimeAgo`
- `useI18n`

It does **NOT** expose any dialog or toast primitive. The host already has them at `@nous-research/ui/ui/components/{dialog,confirm-dialog,toast}` and `@nous-research/ui/hooks/{use-toast,use-confirm-delete}` (verified — components are mounted in `web/src/components/DeleteConfirmDialog.tsx` and used throughout `web/src/pages/{ChannelsPage,FilesPage,PairingPage}.tsx`).

Fix is two additive PRs:

1. **`PR #1` — SDK surface expansion** (`web/src/plugins/registry.ts`): expose `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `DialogHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogFooter`, `DialogClose`, `ConfirmDialog`, `useToast`, `useConfirmDelete`. Update `web/src/plugins/sdk.d.ts:127-135` to document the new entries. `SDK_CONTRACT_VERSION` (`registry.ts:98`) does NOT need a bump — `sdk.d.ts:23-25` explicitly states additive changes don't require one. Independently mergeable; every plugin benefits. (Filed as PR #50550 — the first of two PRs in this branch.)

2. **`PR #2` — Kanban plugin migration** (`plugins/kanban/dashboard/dist/index.js`): replace all 12 `window.{alert,confirm,prompt}` sites with SDK-backed components. Add a `CompletionSummaryDialog` component (textarea + auto-focus + Cmd/Ctrl+Enter + dual-validation). Add a bulk-many `BulkActionDialog` with expandable per-task summary fields. Add 3 new i18n keys under `web/src/i18n/en.ts` for bulk-many copy: `confirmDoneMany`, `confirmArchiveMany`, `confirmBlockedMany`. Existing `tx()` i18n strings (`confirmDone`, `confirmArchive`, `confirmBlocked`, `trash.confirm`, `trash.confirmMany`, `completionSummary`, `completionSummaryRequired`, `archiveBoardConfirm`, `confirmRemoveAttachment`) are all already in `web/src/i18n/en.ts` and need no changes. (Will be a second PR on the same branch, #50550's successor.)

Both PRs drafted on branch `fix/kanban-native-dialogs` in the DavidMetcalfe fork. Design review captured in `docs/design/kanban-dialogs/index.html` on that branch.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

See "Root Cause Analysis" — two additive PRs. The recommended design ("Variant B-refined" in the prototype) is in the prototype HTML — open it in a browser to evaluate.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Feature Feedback]: Desktop composer image layout & preview improvements
items.body:
## 问题描述

使用 Hermes Desktop 时，图片发送体验有两个影响效率的问题：

---

### 问题 1：多图在输入框中纵向排列，浪费右侧大量空白空间

**现象：**
当在输入框（composer）中粘贴/拖入多张图片时，这些图片缩略图是纵向（垂直）一排排布的，而右侧明明有大量空白空间可以横向排列。

**期望行为：**
多张图片应自动换行横向排列（flex-wrap），充分利用可用宽度，让用户无需滚动就能看到所有待发送的图片缩略图。

**示意图：**
```
当前（纵向）                   期望（横向自动换行）
┌─────────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────────┐
│ [图片1]              │       │ [图片1] [图片2]      │
│ [图片2]              │       │ [图片3]              │
│ [图片3]              │       │                     │
│ 描述你需要什么...     │       │ 描述你需要什么...     │
└─────────────────────┘       └─────────────────────┘
```

---

### 问题 2：点击输入框中的图片仅能在右侧栏打开，无法放大查看

**现象：**
在输入框中点击某张图片缩略图，该图片只会在右侧的「文件/工作区」面板中打开显示为一个普通文件，没有缩放/放大功能，缩略图较小时根本看不清图片内容，难以确认是否选对了图。

**期望行为：**
点击输入框中的图片缩略图应弹出可缩放的大图预览（lightbox/overlay 模态框），支持放大、缩小、平移查看图片细节，就像在已发送消息中点击图片的行为一样（注：已发送消息的 lightbox 也有 #39102 描述的闪烁问题，但机制本身是正确的方向）。

---

### 复现环境

- Hermes Desktop（Windows 桌面版）
- 操作系统：Windows 10
- 输入框（composer）中粘贴或拖入多张图片后即可观察到

### 建议方案

1. **图片排列**：将 composer 中图片容器的 CSS 从纵向排列改为 `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; flex-direction: row`，给图片缩略图设置固定尺寸（如 120px），让多图自动横向换行排列。
2. **图片预览**：点击 composer 中的图片缩略图时，复用已有的 lightbox 组件（或类似的 ImageViewer 组件），而不是在右侧文件面板中打开。如果右侧面板仍有必要保留，可改为双击打开面板、单击打开 lightbox。

### 截图

用户提供的全屏截图可在此处查看：
`C:\Users\LinAn\OneDrive\图片\Screenshots\Snipaste_2026-06-22_09-19-42.png`

截图中可见输入框中两张图片纵向排列，右侧有大量空白区域未使用。

items.title: Windows: session cwd in native format breaks terminal tool

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes is started from PowerShell or cmd.exe on Windows, `os.getcwd()` returns a Windows native path which gets stored as the session working directory. Both `init_session()` and `_wrap_command()` in `tools/environments/base.py` embed this path directly into bash scripts via `cd`, but Git Bash cannot parse Windows drive-letter paths.

**Result:** Every terminal tool call fails immediately with exit code 126, `cd: ...: No such file or directory`. File tools, terminal tools, and any tool that executes shell commands are all broken from the first message of a session. The agent is forced to waste tokens diagnosing the false failure, may produce incorrect results, and can fail entirely on tasks requiring shell execution.

## Root Cause

`_msys_to_windows_path()` (in `local.py`) converts MSYS paths to Windows native format for `Popen(cwd=...)`. No reverse helper existed. When the initial cwd is already Windows native (PowerShell/cmd.exe), it passes verbatim into bash `cd` commands and fails.

## Fix

Add `_windows_to_msys_path()` to `BaseEnvironment`: `C:\Users\x` -> `/c/Users/x`. Apply in `init_session()` and `_wrap_command()`. No-op on non-Windows or already-Msys paths.

PR ready.

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

The hermes-agent skill's own SKILL.md (the reference every Hermes agent reads for slash commands) documents two commands that don't exist in the v0.17 command registry:

### 1. `/skill <name>` — doesn't exist

Listed under "Tools & Skills" slash commands as:
```
/skill <name>        Load a skill into session
```

There is no `CommandDef("skill", ...)` in `hermes_cli/commands.py`. The only skills-related slash command is `/skills` (plural), which opens the interactive skills UI.

### 2. `/q` incorrectly listed as `/quit` alias

The Exit section documents:
```
/quit (/exit, /q)    Exit CLI
```

In the actual command registry (`hermes_cli/commands.py:106-107`):
- `/queue` has alias `q`
- `/quit` has alias `exit` only

So `/q` queues a prompt, not exits. The docs should read `/quit (/exit)`.

## Impact

Every Hermes instance reads this file as its own documentation. These phantom commands get propagated into every session's system prompt. Agents may suggest `/skill` or `/q` to users, leading to confusion.

## Fix

- Remove the `/skill <name>` line
- Change `/quit (/exit, /q)` to `/quit (/exit)`

## File

`skills/autonomous-ai-agents/hermes-agent/SKILL.md` (lines ~297 and ~343 in v0.17)

## Description

Skills that declare `platforms: [linux, macos, windows]` in their frontmatter use `python3` in their shell command examples. On Windows, `python3` does not exist — only `python` is available. This means copy-pasted examples from these skills fail on Windows.

## Affected skills (non-exhaustive)

| Skill | Approx. occurrences |

| github-repo-management | ~10 |
| github-code-review | ~5 |
| github-issues | ~7 |
| github-pr-workflow | ~5 |
| arxiv | ~10 |
| maps | ~21 |
| airtable | ~20 |
| ascii-art | ~5 |
| comfyui | ~21 |
| ocr-and-documents | 1 (mixed — uses both python and python3) |
| p5js | ~2 |
| claude-code | ~2 |
| research-paper-writing | ~3 |
| godmode | ~1 |
| obliteratus | ~2 |

Several skills already document the Windows fix inline (youtube-content and youtube-vault-ingest note "On Windows, use python not python3"), but the commands themselves still use python3.

## Expected fix

Either use `python` universally (works on all three platforms), or document per-platform.

items.title: [Feature]: Expand command-TTS output_format allowlist (m4a/aac/amr/opus)
items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

Command-type TTS providers (`tts.providers.<name>` with `type: command`) validate their `output_format` against a hardcoded allowlist — `COMMAND_TTS_OUTPUT_FORMATS = {"mp3","wav","ogg","flac"}` in `tools/tts_tool.py`. Any other value is **silently** coerced back to `mp3` by `_get_command_tts_output_format()`.

This blocks common, useful containers/codecs that a user's command (e.g. an `ffmpeg` pipeline) can trivially produce:

- **`m4a` (AAC)** — the most portable format for sending voice files to WeChat / iOS / general mobile.
- **`aac`**, **`opus`** (standalone), **`amr`** — telephony/voice-optimized formats.

Because the coercion is silent, the framework hands the command an output path with a `.mp3` extension while the command writes (say) `.m4a`, so the post-run existence check at the configured path fails or the file ends up mislabeled. There is no config-only way to get these formats — the only workaround is locally patching `tools/tts_tool.py`, which is lost on every `hermes update`.

## Proposed Solution

Expand the allowlist to the common formats ffmpeg / most TTS CLIs already emit:

```python
COMMAND_TTS_OUTPUT_FORMATS = frozenset(
    {"mp3", "wav", "ogg", "flac", "m4a", "aac", "amr", "opus"}
)
```

This only *permits* a command provider to declare these as `output_format`; it changes no built-in provider's behavior and adds no new required config. The command is still responsible for actually producing the file (e.g. `ffmpeg ... -c:a aac out.m4a`).

## Alternatives Considered

- **Local patch** to the frozenset — works but is wiped by `hermes update`.
- **`output_format: mp3` + external conversion** — defeats the purpose of the TTS tool producing the final artifact, and the agent's `MEDIA:` delivery then ships the wrong format.
- **Per-provider format mapping changes** (cf. open #37337, which fixes OpenAI honoring wav/flac within the current set) — orthogonal; this is specifically about the *command-provider allowlist*.

## Feature Type

Configuration option

## Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

## Contribution

I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR.

items.title: [Windows] dashboard/gateway/desktop backend silently hangs after "Skipping web UI build" — uvicorn never binds (v0.17.0)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

On Windows 10 (native, no WSL), `hermes dashboard`, `hermes gateway run`, and `hermes desktop` all silently hang after printing the "Skipping web UI build" message. The Python process stays alive (~130MB memory) but never reaches the uvicorn bind/serve phase. No port is bound (dashboard) or the port is "LISTENING" in netstat but TCP handshake fails (gateway). `hermes status` reports ✓ running based on PID liveness, which is misleading.

The CLI mode (`hermes -z "..." --cli` and `hermes chat`) works perfectly with the same configuration, so the issue is isolated to the backend server startup path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes Agent v0.17.0 on Windows 10 (native PowerShell, no WSL)
2. Configure any provider API key (DeepSeek in this case) in `.env` and `config.yaml`
3. Run any of:
   - `hermes dashboard --port 9119 --no-open --skip-build --isolated`
   - `hermes gateway run --accept-hooks`
   - `hermes desktop`
4. Observe the process prints at most one line, then hangs indefinitely

## Expected Behavior

After "Skipping web UI build", the dashboard should print `HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY port=9119` and `Hermes Web UI → http://127.0.0.1:9119`, then serve HTTP requests on the bound port.

## Actual Behavior

### Dashboard
→ Skipping web UI build (--skip-build); using dist at C:\Users\jsjyz\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\hermes_cli\web_dist

← hangs here forever, no further output, no port bound

### Gateway
No stdout/stderr at all (gateway-manual.log is 0 bytes)
netstat shows 127.0.0.1:<random_port> LISTENING
but curl and PowerShell Test-NetConnection both fail (TcpTestSucceeded: False)

### Desktop (Electron GUI)
[hermes] [boot] Starting Hermes backend via existing Hermes CLI at C:\Users\jsjyz\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\hermes.EXE [hermes] [boot] Waiting for Hermes backend to launch [hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Timed out waiting for Hermes backend port announcement (90000ms)

(repeated 56+ times in desktop.log)

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10 AMD64 (native, no WSL)
- **Python**: 3.11.15 (venv active)
- **Hermes**: v0.17.0 [e448b214] (2026-06-21)
- **OpenAI SDK**: 2.24.0
- **Provider**: DeepSeek (`deepseek/deepseek-chat`) — CLI mode works perfectly
- **Hermes Home**: `C:\Users\jsjyz\AppData\Local\hermes`

## Key Debugging Findings

### 1. safe-mode does NOT bypass the hang
```bash
PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 timeout 15 hermes --safe-mode dashboard --port 9119 --no-open --skip-build --isolated < /dev/null
Output:

→ Skipping web UI build (--skip-build); using dist at C:\Users\jsjyz\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\hermes_cli\web_dist
# ← killed by timeout after 15s, no further output
This rules out:

❌ Plugin discovery (safe-mode disables all plugins)
❌ Interactive auth setup (stdin = /dev/null)
❌ os.execvpe Windows bug (v0.17.0 already has the fix from PR #44355 at main.py:11225)
❌ active_profile sticky state (file does not exist on this system)
2. The hang location is between these code points
main.py:11272 — prints "Skipping web UI build" ✓ (this prints)
main.py:11279 — discover_plugins() ← possibly hangs here, or after
main.py:11293 — start_background_mcp_discovery() ← possibly hangs here
main.py:11328 — start_server() → web_server.py:12935 → uvicorn.Server.startup() ← never reached
3. Process state during hang
Python process alive, ~130MB memory
No CPU activity (0%)
No thread appears to be in a busy loop
dashboard.log / gateway-manual.log are 0 bytes (no stdout/stderr captured)
4. agent.log shows incomplete startup
INFO hermes_cli.plugins: Plugin discovery complete: 49 found, 42 enabled
INFO hermes_cli.web_server: Mounted plugin API routes: /api/plugins/hermes-achievements/
INFO hermes_cli.web_server: Mounted plugin API routes: /api/plugins/kanban/
# ← no uvicorn startup banner, no "Uvicorn running on..." log
Comparison with Known Windows Issues
Issue	Status	Relation to this bug
#43429 — WSL2 Desktop backend timeout	Open	Different: their backend actually starts (curl returns 200), only Electron IPC times out. Our backend never responds at all.
#44318 — Windows 11 update breaks startup	Closed	Different: caused by active_profile + os.execvpe. Fix (PR #44355) is already in v0.17.0. Our active_profile doesn't exist.
PR #44355 — skip dashboard re-exec on Windows	Merged	Already in v0.17.0 (main.py:11225). Does not fix this bug.
This appears to be a new, unreported Windows-specific bug.

Excluded Causes
✅ API key configured (DeepSeek works in CLI mode)
✅ Python venv healthy, all required packages installed
✅ Config version latest (v30)
✅ Windows firewall has python.exe inbound allow rule
✅ Port not in Windows excluded port range
✅ All zombie processes killed before retry, issue reproduces consistently
✅ active_profile file does not exist (not the #44318 root cause)
✅ PR #44355 fix already present (not the #44282 root cause)
Debug Reports (6-hour expiry)
Main report: https://dpaste.com/BAMDSRG9U
agent.log: https://dpaste.com/8STA9WALV
gui.log: https://paste.rs/CADsp
desktop.log: https://paste.rs/6612d
Workaround
CLI mode works perfectly:

bash
hermes -z "your question" --yolo --cli
hermes chat
Suggested Investigation
The Hermes team may want to check:

Whether discover_plugins() (called explicitly at main.py:11279 for dashboard) hangs on Windows even in safe-mode (perhaps a plugin's register() blocks on a network call or lock)
Whether start_background_mcp_discovery() at main.py:11293 has a Windows-specific deadlock (it spawns a thread — possible fork/thread issue on Windows)
Whether uvicorn.Server.startup() has a Windows asyncio event loop issue (ProactorEventLoop vs SelectorEventLoop)
Adding a print() statement between each step in cmd_dashboard() (lines 11270-11330) to pinpoint the exact hang location
Willing to Submit a PR?
Yes — willing to help test any proposed fix on this Windows 10 environment.

items.title: [Bug]: Feishu/Lark group @mention messages not delivered — WebSocket never receives group events
items.body:
## Bug Description

The Feishu/Lark bot can receive direct messages and bot-added-to-group events normally, but **group @mention messages never arrive at the gateway**. The Feishu WebSocket simply doesnt push group message events to the bot.

I have verified:
- Bot capability is enabled ✅
- `im.message.receive_v1` event is subscribed (WebSocket/long-connection mode) ✅
- All required permissions enabled: `im:message.group_at_msg:readonly`, `im:message.group_at_msg.include_bot:readonly`, `im:message.p2p_msg:readonly`, `im:message:send_as_bot` ✅
- Version published with "All employees" scope ✅
- Bot is successfully added to the group ✅ (`Bot added to chat:` appears in logs)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Feishu bot app via `hermes gateway setup` (scan-to-create)
2. Configure it with the scan-to-create defaults (which include all necessary permissions and event subscriptions)
3. Publish the app (version 1.0.1 → 1.0.2 with all-employee scope)
4. Create a group chat in Feishu, add the bot to the group
5. @mention the bot in the group (e.g. `@Hermes hello`)
6. Observe gateway.log — the group message event never arrives

## Expected Behavior

When a user @mentions the bot in a group chat, the Feishu WebSocket should push an `im.message.receive_v1` event to the gateway, and the adapter should process and respond to it.

## Actual Behavior

Only DM messages and bot-added/removed events are received. Group messages are completely absent from gateway.log — no error, no warning, no rejection log. The events simply never arrive.

Gateway log excerpt showing the pattern:
```
[Feishu] Bot added to chat: oc_4fd3622a8cac71d37978549be10ba77c
[Feishu] Inbound dm message received: ... chat_id=oc_b76d8ecf3bd2307aa50bbe0beb05cced
```
No "Inbound group message received" ever appears.

## Diagnostic Steps Taken

1. Confirmed all permissions, event subscriptions, and publish status on Feishu Open Platform
2. Upgraded `lark-oapi` from 1.5.3 → 1.6.8 (latest) — no change
3. Restarted gateway multiple times — no change
4. Changed bot availability scope from "some members" to "all employees" — no change

## Root Cause Analysis

The Hermes Feishu adapter uses the **old event dispatcher pattern** (`register_p2_im_message_receive_v1` from `lark_oapi.event.dispatcher_handler`) rather than the **Channel SDK** (`lark_oapi.channel.FeishuChannel`) introduced in lark-oapi 1.6.0.

Per the [Feishu developer docs](https://open.feishu.cn/document/mcp_open_tools/integrating-agents-with-feishu/overview), the **Channel SDK** is the recommended approach for agents that need group chat, DM, and doc comment interaction. The Channel SDK (`lark_oapi.channel`) was introduced specifically to handle these interaction patterns correctly.

The relevant code is in:
`plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py` — uses `EventDispatcherHandler.builder().register_p2_im_message_receive_v1(self._on_message_event)` instead of the newer Channel SDK API.

Additionally, the bug report template is missing "Feishu/Lark" from the "Messaging Platform" dropdown — it should be added alongside Telegram, Discord, Slack, and WhatsApp.

## Environment

- **OS**: macOS 26.5.1
- **Python**: 3.11.15
- **Hermes**: v0.17.0 (2026.6.19)
- **lark-oapi**: was 1.5.3, upgraded to 1.6.8 — no change

## Debug Report

- Report: https://paste.rs/X65j7
- agent.log: https://paste.rs/uXEjE
- gateway.log: https://paste.rs/IWz3f

## Related Issues

- #5465 — Support require_mention: false for group chats in Feishu
- #23698 — Feishu: group message replies routed to senders DM instead of group chat
- #25728 — Buffer unmentioned Feishu/Lark group messages

items.title: Security: optional CubeSandbox terminal backend for isolated shell/code execution

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
### Problem

Hermes today runs `terminal` and `execute_code` on the **same host process** when `terminal.backend` is `local` (the common gateway / container deployment). That is convenient for file tools and workspace persistence, but it means model-generated shell and Python execute **on the Hermes host** unless operators switch the *entire* terminal backend to Docker, Modal, Daytona, etc.

For deployments that already run a **CubeSandbox** (E2B-compatible KVM microVM) control plane, we need a first-class integration that:

1. Keeps **low-risk file tools** on the durable host workspace.
2. Routes **high-risk tools** (`terminal`, `execute_code`) into **hardware-isolated microVMs**.
3. **Fails closed** when Cube is unreachable — no silent downgrade to host execution in production configs.

### Proposed solution

Add **`cube_sandbox`** as the seventh terminal backend (`e2b-code-interpreter==2.8.0`, optional `hermes-agent[cube]` extra), plus a **split-mode plugin** when `SANDBOX_TYPE=cube`:

| Mode | Config | Behavior |
|------|--------|----------|
| **Direct** | `terminal.backend: cube_sandbox` | All terminal + `execute_code` in microVM |
| **Split (recommended)** | `SANDBOX_TYPE=cube` + `terminal.backend: local` | Plugin overrides `terminal` + `execute_code` only; file tools stay on host workspace with host↔VM sync for touched paths |

Shared pieces:

- `check_cube_sandbox_requirements()` — one credential/SDK gate for direct backend and plugin `check_fn`
- Session VM key: `{HERMES_INSTANCE_NAME}-{session_id}`
- `cube_sandbox` in remote-backend prompt hints and approval skip list (commands already run in VM)

### Security / ops notes

- **Do not** set `CUBE_FALLBACK_BACKEND` in production (dev-only downgrade when control plane is down).
- Optional `SANDBOX_TOKEN_API_URL` path for short-lived keys; static `CUBE_API_KEY` supported for transitional deployments.
- Workspace sync: conservative push (`touched` paths), default pull after successful terminal (`after_terminal`, full workspace scope).

### Out of scope (this issue)

- Building or operating the CubeSandbox cluster itself
- Downstream platform deployment wiring outside Hermes core
- New core file tools — only routing + sync hooks in `file_tools.py`

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pip install "hermes-agent[cube]"` (or `[cube]` extra) installs pinned `e2b-code-interpreter==2.8.0`
- [ ] Direct mode: `TERMINAL_ENV=cube_sandbox` + `CUBE_API_URL` / `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID` / credentials → terminal and `execute_code` run in microVM
- [ ] Split mode: `SANDBOX_TYPE=cube`, `TERMINAL_ENV=local`, plugin enabled → file tools on host; terminal/code in VM; touched-path sync works
- [ ] Split mode fail-closed: with Cube control plane down, `read_file`/`write_file` still work; `terminal` errors (no host fallback)
- [ ] Tests: `tests/tools/test_cube_*.py`, `tests/plugins/test_cube_sandbox_plugin.py`, plus related terminal/approval/prompt_builder regressions
- [ ] Docs: `configuration.md`, `tools.md`, README seventh-backend mention

### Implementation

PR: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/47614

Author has rebased onto latest `main`, resolved the sole merge conflict in `tools/file_tools.py` (kept upstream `write_file` line-number guard + cube `file_tool_hook`), and re-run tests locally.

### Reviewer quick path (~5 min)

1. `plugins/cube_sandbox/` — plugin overrides `terminal` + `execute_code` when `SANDBOX_TYPE=cube`
2. `tools/cube_split.py` + `tools/workspace_sync.py` — split switch + host↔VM sync
3. `tools/environments/cube_sandbox.py` — E2B-compatible environment
4. `tools/file_tools.py` — host file ops + touched-path registry (no-op when split off)
5. `tools/terminal_tool.py` — backend factory + cleanup hooks
6. Tests under `tests/tools/test_cube_*.py` and `tests/plugins/test_cube_sandbox_plugin.py`

items.title: [Bug]: [gateway] Agent cache invalidates and resets /usage command's API calls and token counters to 0 on some follow-up turns
items.body:
### Bug Description

When using the gateway (WhatsApp, etc.), the agent cache is invalidated intermittently due to a stale `message_count` mismatch. When this happens, a new `AIAgent` is built with all session counters (`session_api_calls`, `session_input_tokens`, `session_output_tokens`, `session_cache_read_tokens`, etc.) reset to 0, making the `/usage` command report a severe undercount of API calls and token usage.

The invalidation is probabilistic, it fires most reliably after turns with large flushes (multi-tool responses, context compression), and rarely on simple text-only replies.

Affects gateway mode only; CLI mode uses a single agent instance per session and is unaffected.

### Steps to Reproduce

- Start a gateway session (e.g., WhatsApp DM)
- Send a message that triggers a multi-tool response (5+ API calls) or any response large enough to slow the DB flush
- Send any follow-up message
- Run `/usage`, observe token counts and API calls are severely underreported (only counts calls since the rebuild)
- Repeat, invalidation may or may not fire on subsequent turns depending on flush timing

### Expected Behavior

`/usage` should report the cumulative API call count and token totals for the entire session since its start, regardless of whether the agent cache was invalidated and rebuilt mid-session.

### Actual Behavior

`/usage` reports only the API calls and token totals accumulated since the most recent agent cache rebuild. All prior counters are lost because the new `AIAgent` initializes them to 0 and does not backfill from the SessionDB.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

WhatsApp

### Debug Report

```shell
-
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

0.17.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Logs from affected sessions


2026-06-20 13:55:01,707 INFO gateway.run: Invalidated run generation for agent:main:whatsapp:dm:*** → 33 (session_reset)
2026-06-20 13:57:09,855 INFO gateway.run: response ready: platform=whatsapp chat=... time=116.7s api_calls=5 response=3809 chars
2026-06-20 13:58:11,828 INFO gateway.run: inbound message: ... msg='answer in eng'
2026-06-20 13:58:12,414 INFO gateway.run: Agent cache invalidated for session agent:main:whatsapp:dm:***: message_count changed (14 -> 15), possible cross-process write
2026-06-20 13:59:00,273 INFO gateway.run: response ready: platform=whatsapp chat=... time=48.4s api_calls=1 response=3796 chars
2026-06-20 14:03:50,141 INFO gateway.run: response ready: platform=whatsapp chat=... time=59.1s api_calls=1 response=2247 chars


`/usage` at 14:06 showed `API calls: 2` (only post-rebuild calls), while DB recorded `api_call_count: 7` (correct cumulative total).


2026-06-21 08:33:23,518 INFO gateway.run: Agent cache invalidated for session agent:main:whatsapp:dm:***: message_count changed (2 -> 3), possible cross-process write
2026-06-21 10:38:42,528 INFO [20260621_084515_20dd5b89] gateway.run: Agent cache invalidated for session agent:main:whatsapp:dm:***: message_count changed (14 -> 15), possible cross-process write
2026-06-21 13:14:57,162 INFO [20260621_122327_c37ab529] gateway.run: Agent cache invalidated for session agent:main:whatsapp:dm:***: message_count changed (8 -> 9), possible cross-process write
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

1. Stale message_count triggers false cache invalidation (probabilistic)

After a turn completes, the gateway caches the agent with the DB's current `message_count`. The agent thread then flushes its turn messages to the DB, incrementing `message_count`. On the next inbound message, the gateway compares the stale cached count against the now-higher DB count and concludes "possible cross-process write" → invalidates the agent.

This is not a cross-process write, it's the agent's own DB flush racing with the cache write. The ordering is:

```
Turn finishes → gateway caches agent (message_count=14)
             → agent thread flushes messages to DB → message_count becomes 15
Next message  → gateway sees 14 ≠ 15 → invalidates cache
```

When the race fires:

- After large flushes (multi-tool responses, compression): high probability, flush takes longer than the cache write window
- After simple text replies: low probability, flush completes too quickly to be caught mid-window

Gateway logs across 17 invalidations over 5 days confirm this pattern, invalidations cluster around tool-heavy turns and compression events:

```
[session] Agent cache invalidated: message_count changed (184 -> 192), possible cross-process write  # compression
[session] Agent cache invalidated: message_count changed (14 -> 15), possible cross-process write     # after tool loop
[session] Agent cache invalidated: message_count changed (12 -> 13), possible cross-process write     # after tool loop
[session] Agent cache invalidated: message_count changed (7 -> 8), possible cross-process write       # after tool loop
```

### 2. All session counters reset to 0 on agent rebuild

When a new `AIAgent` is created for an existing (non-`/new`) session, `agent_init.py` initializes all session counters to 0 without backfilling from the DB row's cumulative values:

```python
# agent/agent_init.py:1657-1660
agent.session_api_calls = 0
agent.session_input_tokens = 0
agent.session_output_tokens = 0
agent.session_cache_read_tokens = 0
```

The DB correctly tracks cumulative API calls via `COALESCE(api_call_count, 0) + 1`, so the DB always has the right total, but the `/usage` command reads from the in-memory agent counters:

```python
# gateway/slash_commands.py:3355-3357
input_tokens = getattr(agent, "session_input_tokens", 0) or 0
output_tokens = getattr(agent, "session_output_tokens", 0) or 0
cache_read = getattr(agent, "session_cache_read_tokens", 0) or 0
```

**Relevant code paths:**

- `agent/agent_init.py:1657` — all session counters initialized to 0 on init
- `agent/conversation_loop.py:1846-1853` — session counters incremented per API call
- `gateway/run.py:15410-15480` — message_count mismatch detection and cache eviction
- `gateway/run.py:15426` — cache lookup with stale message_count snapshot
- `gateway/run.py:13717` — `_refresh_agent_cache_message_count` definition
- `gateway/slash_commands.py:3274-3370` — `/usage` reads in-memory session counters
- `hermes_state.py:1661` — DB: `api_call_count = COALESCE(api_call_count, 0) + ?` (incremental)
- `hermes_state.py:1640` — DB: `api_call_count = ?` (absolute mode)

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## 问题描述

运行 `pytest` 测试套件时，测试创建的 fake session（Telegram/Matrix/CLI 等）会写入用户的**真实** `~/.hermes/state.db`，导致仪表盘上出现大量"无标题会话"（0 消息、无 model、无标题）。

实测一次 pytest 跑完产生了 **187 个空壳 session**，全部污染进生产库。

## 根因

`hermes_state.py` 第 108 行：

```python
DEFAULT_DB_PATH = get_hermes_home() / "state.db"
```

这是一个**模块级常量**，在 Python import 时立即求值。而 conftest.py 的 `_hermetic_environment` fixture 通过 `monkeypatch.setenv("HERMES_HOME", tmp_path)` 做隔离——但 fixture 在 import **之后**才执行，`DEFAULT_DB_PATH` 已经被冻结为 `~/.hermes/state.db`。

后续 `SessionDB.__init__`（第 681 行）：
```python
self.db_path = db_path or DEFAULT_DB_PATH
```
不传 `db_path` 时就命中了这个冻结的生产路径。

### 证据

1. 部分测试文件已知道这个问题并手动 patch：
   ```python
   # tests/gateway/test_session_dm_thread_seeding.py 注释：
   # "DEFAULT_DB_PATH is a module-level constant computed ... at import time"
   monkeypatch.setattr(hermes_state, "DEFAULT_DB_PATH", tmp_path / "state.db")
   ```
2. 但并非所有测试都做了这个 patch，未 patch 的测试就会泄漏到生产库。

## 修复方案

将 `DEFAULT_DB_PATH` 从模块级常量改为惰性求值函数：

```python
# hermes_state.py
# Before:
DEFAULT_DB_PATH = get_hermes_home() / "state.db"

# After:
def _default_db_path() -> Path:
    return get_hermes_home() / "state.db"

# 保留向后兼容的模块级属性（供 monkeypatch.setattr 等外部引用）
DEFAULT_DB_PATH = property(lambda self: _default_db_path())  # 或用 __getattr__
```

`SessionDB.__init__` 改为：
```python
self.db_path = db_path or _default_db_path()
```

同时需要检查 `session_search_tool.py`、`hermes_cli/main.py` 等其他引用点。

## 影响范围

- `hermes_state.py:108` — DEFAULT_DB_PATH 定义
- `hermes_state.py:681` — SessionDB.__init__
- `tools/session_search_tool.py:622-623` — 引用 DEFAULT_DB_PATH
- `hermes_cli/main.py:12151-12156` — 引用 DEFAULT_DB_PATH
- `acp_adapter/session.py:408` — 注释引用
- 多个测试文件中的 monkeypatch.setattr 调用需同步适配

items.title: [Feature]: Add GLM-5 reasoning support to direct ZAI provider

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

I'm trying to use Hermes' direct `zai` / `glm` provider with GLM-5.x models and the `/reasoning` controls, but the current provider path appears to ignore them.

Right now `plugins/model-providers/zai/__init__.py` registers a plain `ProviderProfile` with no `build_api_kwargs_extras()` override. On the chat-completions transport path, that means Hermes has no ZAI-specific logic to forward GLM reasoning controls at all, so `/reasoning high`, `/reasoning off`, `minimal`, `max`, etc. do not have a direct-provider mapping.

This is different from the `opencode-go` relay path covered by #49279 / PR #50694. That path now has its own GLM-5 reasoning mapping, but the direct `zai` provider still does not.

From the official GLM docs:
- GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.1 / GLM-5 / GLM-4.7 default to Thinking-on behavior
- `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` is the documented way to turn thinking off
- `reasoning_effort` is documented for GLM-5.2 and above, with values including `max`, `xhigh`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `minimal`, and `none`

So the direct provider already has an upstream capability surface to map to; Hermes just doesn't currently expose it on this route.

## Proposed Solution

Add a dedicated `ZAIProfile` override in `plugins/model-providers/zai/__init__.py` (or a shared mixin reused across GLM-capable routes) that translates Hermes `reasoning_config` into the native GLM request fields.

Concretely:
- When reasoning is disabled, emit top-level `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`
- For GLM-5.2+ models, map Hermes effort levels onto top-level `reasoning_effort`
- Follow the documented GLM compatibility semantics rather than inventing a new Hermes-only mapping
- Add focused unit coverage for the direct `zai` provider plus final transport kwargs

A minimal version could start with GLM-5.2 / 5.1 / 5 and leave older model-family nuance to follow-up tests if needed.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep using `opencode-go` for GLM reasoning
  - This works around the problem for one relay, but it does not help users who want Hermes' first-class direct Z.AI provider path.
- Use `custom` instead of `zai`
  - This loses the direct-provider path entirely and still leaves Hermes without a proper built-in GLM reasoning contract on `zai`.
- Leave direct `zai` without reasoning controls
  - This keeps `/reasoning` behavior inconsistent across GLM routes and makes the curated direct provider weaker than relay-specific integrations.

## Feature Type

Other

## Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

## Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

## Debug Report (optional)

N/A — this is based on provider-path code inspection plus the official GLM capability docs, not a local crash/install problem.

References:
- https://docs.bigmodel.cn/cn/guide/capabilities/thinking-mode
- https://docs.bigmodel.cn/cn/guide/start/concept-param
- Related direct-neighbor issue: #49279
- Related PR on the relay path: #50694

items.title: Hermes translation of `extra_body` strips top-level `chat_template_kwargs` for NVIDIA NIM, preventing thinking_mode from reaching the main M3 model

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
# Hermes translation of `extra_body` strips top-level `chat_template_kwargs` for NVIDIA NIM, preventing thinking_mode from reaching the main M3 model

## TL;DR

When configuring `chat_template_kwargs.thinking_mode: enabled` on the **main** (orchestrator)
model `minimaxai/minimax-m3` over NVIDIA NIM via the `auxiliary.*.extra_body` config block —
or via `BaseChatCompletionsTransport._build_kwargs_from_profile()`'s `extra_body` assembly
path — the parameter never reaches the NIM endpoint. Result: `reasoning_content` is
empty in the response and the desktop GUI never renders the thinking block.

The behavior is **deterministic and reproducible** with a 5-line `urllib` probe against
NVIDIA NIM (provided below). Fixing it requires Hermes to expose a **top-level
passthrough mechanism** (not just an `extra_body` wrapper) for `chat_template_kwargs`,
or to detect NIM/M3 as a known provider needing top-level keys.

## Environment

- **Hermes commit**: `e493b1c48…`  (note: file/line numbers below assume current `main`; pin via `git rev-parse HEAD` when reproducing from a clone)
- **Local path**: `~/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent/` (Windows)
- **Model**: `minimaxai/minimax-m3` (NVIDIA NIM)
- **Provider**: `nvidia` (`https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions`)
- **Subsystem affected**: desktop GUI reasoning-block rendering, main orchestrator reasoning, any future consumer that wraps thinking config via `extra_body`

## Config that triggers the bug

```yaml
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml (excerpt)
model:
  default: minimaxai/minimax-m3
  provider: nvidia

delegation:
  model: moonshotai/kimi-k2.6
  provider: nvidia

auxiliary:
  vision:
    provider: nvidia
    model: moonshotai/kimi-k2.6
    extra_body:
      chat_template_kwargs:
        thinking: true
      reasoning_budget: 8192
```

The orchestrator reaches M3 with `thinking_mode` going through the `extra_body` assembly path
(`agent/transports/chat_completions.py:598`). For M3 this fails; for Kimi it silently ignores.

## Repro steps — single-shot Python probe (no Hermes agent involved)

Copy this verbatim into a `~/probe_nim_thinking.py` (replace `NVIDIA_API_KEY`):

```python
import os, json, urllib.request

key = os.environ["NVIDIA_API_KEY"]
def post(payload):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions",
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + key, "Content-Type": "application/json"},
        method="POST",
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
        return r.status, json.loads(r.read().decode())

prompt = "Spiegami in 5 righe perché il ghiaccio galleggia sull'acqua."

# === VARIANT A — canonical NVIDIA docs (top-level chat_template_kwargs) ===
status_a, j_a = post({
    "model": "minimaxai/minimax-m3",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    "max_tokens": 8192, "temperature": 1.00, "top_p": 0.95, "stream": False,
    "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking_mode": "enabled"},
})
print("VARIANT A (top-level chat_template_kwargs):")
print("  status =", status_a, " reasoning_content present =",
      bool(j_a.get("choices",[{}])[0].get("message",{}).get("reasoning_content")))
print("  → EXPECT: status=200, reasoning_content populated")
print()

# === VARIANT B — what Hermes actually sends (extra_body wrapping) ===
status_b, j_b = post({
    "model": "minimaxai/minimax-m3",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    "max_tokens": 8192, "temperature": 1.00, "top_p": 0.95, "stream": False,
    "extra_body": {
        "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking_mode": "enabled"},
        "reasoning_budget": 8192,
    },
})
print("VARIANT B (extra_body wrapping as Hermes does):")
print("  raw response =", json.dumps(j_b)[:400])
print("  → EXPECT on M3: HTTP 400 'Unsupported parameter: extra_body'")
```

### Observed output (my environment, 2026-06-22)

```
VARIANT A (top-level chat_template_kwargs):
  status = 200  reasoning_content present = True
  → reasoning_content: "The user is asking me to explain in 5 lines why ice floats on water,
                        in Italian. This is a straightforward physics/chemistry question..."
  → content:            "Il ghiaccio galleggia sull'acqua perché è meno denso dell'acqua..."

VARIANT B (extra_body wrapping as Hermes does):
  raw response = {"message":"Validation: Unsupported parameter(s): `extra_body`",
                  "type":"Bad Request","code":400}
```

## Root cause (with file:line references)

**File**: `agent/transports/chat_completions.py`
**Lines 543–598** (current `main`):

```python
# extra_body assembly
extra_body: dict[str, Any] = {}

# Profile's extra_body (tags, provider prefs, vl_high_resolution, etc.)
profile_body = profile.build_extra_body(...)
if profile_body:
    extra_body.update(profile_body)

# Profile's reasoning/thinking extra_body entries
if extra_body_from_profile:
    extra_body.update(extra_body_from_profile)

# ... omitted ...

# Request overrides (user config)
overrides = params.get("request_overrides")
if overrides:
    for k, v in overrides.items():
        if k == "extra_body" and isinstance(v, dict):
            extra_body.update(v)
        else:
            api_kwargs[k] = v

if extra_body:
    # ... Gemini branch omitted ...
    if extra_body:
        api_kwargs["extra_body"] = extra_body
```

Every configured `extra_body.chat_template_kwargs.*` ends up **inside** `api_kwargs["extra_body"]`. For NVIDIA NIM with M3, `extra_body` at the top level of the request body is rejected with HTTP 400. For Kimi on NIM, it is accepted but the inner `chat_template_kwargs` is silently ignored (cf. issue #22949).

The canonical NVIDIA NIM example for M3 ([`build.nvidia.com` Model Card](https://build.nvidia.com/minimax-m3)) shows the parameter at the **top level** of the request body — never inside `extra_body`:

```python
# NVIDIA NIM canonical snippet for M3
payload = {
    "model": "minimaxai/minimax-m3",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": ""}],
    "max_tokens": 8192, "temperature": 1.00, "top_p": 0.95,
    "stream": stream,
    "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking_mode": "enabled"},   # ← top level, not nested
}
```

## Expected vs observed

| | Expected (NVIDIA docs) | Observed today (Hermes) |
|---|---|---|
| `chat_template_kwargs` placement | top-level request body field | wrapped inside `extra_body` |
| M3 NIM response with thinking ON | `reasoning_content` non-null | HTTP 400, request rejected (M3) / `reasoning_content: null` (Kimi, see #22949) |
| Desktop GUI reasoning chevron ▶ | visible under assistant replies | not rendered, no chevron |

## Why other paths in Hermes don't fix this

- `agent.reasoning_effort: medium` controls only the **prompt-injected reasoning_effort string** (added by the system prompt). It does NOT emit `chat_template_kwargs` to the wire payload, nor does it affect NIM's own reasoning tokens.
- `delegation.model: moonshotai/kimi-k2.6` is a different request envelope. Subagent reasoning E2E is partial-covered because of issue #22949.
- `auxiliary.vision.extra_body.chat_template_kwargs` is correctly formatted in config but lost in transport wrapping.

## Suggested fix (config-side, no code change)

Add top-level passthrough for known thinking-tier keys. Two designs:

**Design 1**: per-aux block sibling keys (`auxiliary.vision.chat_template_kwargs` and `auxiliary.vision.reasoning_budget` independently of `extra_body`):

```yaml
auxiliary:
  vision:
    provider: nvidia
    model: moonshotai/kimi-k2.6
    chat_template_kwargs:        # ← new, top-level passthrough
      thinking: true
    reasoning_budget: 8192       # ← new, top-level passthrough
    # extra_body: {} # omitted, NIM doesn't accept it for M3
```

**Design 2**: provider-level whitelist in the NVIDIA profile (`providers/nvidia/__init__.py`):

```python
NIM_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS = {
    "moonshotai/kimi-k2.6": ["chat_template_kwargs", "reasoning_budget"],
    "minimaxai/minimax-m3":  ["chat_template_kwargs"],
}
# Then in transport.before_send, lift these keys from extra_body to api_kwargs.
```

Both designs preserve prompt caching (only payload shape changes, not system prompt content). Both are additive and won't change behavior for other providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Nous) that already accept `extra_body`.

I am happy to open a PR with either design; waiting for maintainer preference before drafting.

## Related issues (already open upstream)

- **#22949** — Kimi K2-6 with `chat_template_kwargs.thinking: true` returns `content: null`, `reasoning_content` not displayed in Telegram. (Kimi-specific; my case is M3-related but the symptom class overlaps.)
- **#35566** — `get_auxiliary_extra_body()` ignores `auxiliary..extra_body`. (Adjacent bug; my case is upstream of that one because the wrapping happens *before* `get_auxiliary_extra_body()` is even reached.)
- **#19883** — `[Feature]: Native reasoning_effort support for NVIDIA NIM` (would paper over the symptom; the deeper fix is passthrough.)
- **#7209** — `support model.extra_body passthrough for CLI and gateway`. (Closest to a clean architectural fix.)

This issue is filed under the specific M3-main + NIM combination with probe evidence; cross-referencing the open issues above to prevent duplicate triage.

## Evidence captured (local files)

- Full probe transcript (5 calls, all 200/400, with diffs): see companion file `evidence/probe_2026-06-22.txt` in this report.
- Hermes source screenshot of the wrapping path: `agent/transports/chat_completions.py` lines 528–598.
- GUI rendering path (for context): `apps/desktop/src/session/hooks/use-message-stream.ts` line 364 — `if (queued.reasoning) { ... }` — confirms the desktop GUI *would* render the block if the payload had `reasoning_content != null`.

[Hermes_issue_2026-06-22_evidence.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29197833/Hermes_issue_2026-06-22_evidence.txt)
