bug: Desktop app sessions saved as source "tui" instead of "desktop"

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
When creating a session from the Hermes Desktop app (Electron), the session is stored in state.db with source = "tui" instead of source = "desktop".

Root cause: 
Desktop app's session.create, session.resume, and branch session.create don't pass source: 'desktop' to tui_gateway. The gateway defaults to "tui" when source is absent (tui_gateway/server.py lines 4201, 4541).

Files affected:
apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.ts
session.create (line 462) — missing source: 'desktop'
session.resume (line 706) — missing source: 'desktop'
branch session.create (line 899) — missing source: 'desktop'

Why this matters:
Desktop sessions indistinguishable from terminal TUI sessions
The app already defines desktop as a valid source in session-source.ts (LABELS, ALIASES, LOCAL_SESSION_SOURCE_IDS)
Makes it impossible to filter/group sessions by platform in WebUI or Desktop sidebar
Fix: Add source: 'desktop' to all three requestGateway(...) calls in use-session-actions.ts.

Workaround for existing sessions: No reliable workaround — sessions created before the fix are permanently labeled tui with no way to distinguish desktop from terminal TUI. After deploying the fix, only new sessions will correctly use source: "desktop". Users who exclusively use the Desktop app can manually UPDATE sessions SET source = 'desktop' WHERE source = 'tui', but this is not safe for users who also use hermes --tui.

Labels: comp/tui, type/bug

items.title: Desktop: model picker persists wrong provider (litellm-proxy → openrouter) + toolsets toggles don't persist

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Report

### Environment
- Hermes Agent: v0.17.0 (f1e6d39a)
- Hermes Desktop: v0.17.0
- OS: Windows 10 + WSL2 Ubuntu
- Profile: default

### Issue 1: Model picker persistence writes wrong provider

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Configure multiple providers in \`config.yaml\`: \`cpa\`, \`litellm-proxy\`, \`ollama\`
2. Open Desktop → Settings → Model, select provider \`litellm-proxy\` and model \`nvidia/nim/deepseek-v4-pro\`
3. Click "Apply" (or use the model picker with "Make global default")
4. Inspect \`config.yaml\`: \`model.provider\` becomes \`openrouter\` instead of \`litellm-proxy\`
5. New sessions get HTTP 400 because \`openrouter\` is not configured

**What happened:**
\`\`\`yaml
# Before (user intent):
model:
  provider: litellm-proxy
  default: nvidia/nim/deepseek-v4-pro

# After Desktop picker persist:
model:
  provider: openrouter    # ❌ catalog inference chose first aggregator
  default: nvidia/nim/deepseek-v4-pro
\`\`\`

**Root cause:**
- \`model-picker.tsx:81-85\` reads \`provider.slug\` from catalog inference (\`hermes_cli/models.py:155-268\`)
- For \`nvidia/nim/*\` prefixed models, catalog matches \`nvidia\` provider first, fails (user has \`litellm-proxy\` not \`nvidia\`), falls back to first aggregator with NIM route = \`openrouter\`
- \`use-model-controls.ts:87\` writes this to \`config.yaml\` without validating the provider exists in user's \`providers:\` block
- Net effect: user's local LiteLLM pool is silently bypassed, requests go to OpenRouter's public NIM

**Related:** #46319, #46320, #43156

### Issue 2: Toolsets toggle in Desktop settings doesn't persist

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Desktop → Skills & Tools → Tool Sets tab
2. Toggle any toolset (e.g., enable "Computer Use", disable "Discord")
3. Click the refresh button in the top-right corner
4. All toggles revert to their previous state

**Expected:** Toolset toggles should persist across page refresh and app restart.

**Actual:** Toggles are ephemeral — they don't write to \`config.yaml\`'s \`agent.disabled_toolsets\`, and Desktop's local state is lost on refresh. The "17/26 enabled" counter is also misleading — it reflects transient local state, not what's actually in config.

**Related:** #44505 (Desktop gateway ignores \`agent.disabled_toolsets\`), #44499 (Desktop ignores BrowserOS MCP config), #4775 (config.yaml silently rewritten with expanded defaults)

### Underlying pattern
Desktop UI settings lack a reliable "raw user config" ↔ "effective runtime config" separation. Multiple code paths (model picker catalog inference, tools config save, \`hermes tools\` wizard) write the resolved/expanded config object back to disk instead of patching only the specific keys the user changed. Also raised in #4775 and PR #3596.

**Suggested fix direction:**
1. \`model-picker.tsx\`: prefer providers the user has actually configured in \`config.yaml\`'s \`providers:\` block over catalog-inferred aggregators
2. \`use-model-controls.ts\`: validate \`selection.provider\` exists in user config before writing \`--global\`
3. Desktop toolsets page: write toggles directly to \`agent.disabled_toolsets\` in \`config.yaml\`
4. Adopt the raw-preserving config save path from #3596 to prevent silent config rewriting

items.title: [Bug]: tools[].function.description (session_search) reaches API with invalid Unicode code point — HTTP 400 across providers

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

Every request fails with a non-retryable HTTP 400 as soon as session_search is among the enabled tools. The failure is provider-agnostic — reproduced on both OpenRouter (minimax/minimax-m3) and DeepSeek (deepseek-v4-pro) with the exact same request body. DeepSeek's API returns a specific parse error pinpointing the cause:

Failed to parse the request body as JSON: tools[9].function.description: invalid unicode code point at line 489 column 2842

tools[9] is the session_search tool. Its description contains the character ± (U+00B1) — e.g. "...±5 message window around the match...".

Reproduced a second time after updating Hermes (request grew from ~3,930 to ~22,684 tokens due to more context/tools loaded). The error persisted on the same field, just at a different position since the file grew:

Failed to parse the request body as JSON: tools[9].function.description: invalid unicode code point at line 516 column 3713

This confirms the bug is not related to conversation length or token count — it's tied specifically to the session_search tool's description field, regardless of how large the surrounding request is.

What I've ruled out


The source file is clean. tools/session_search_tool.py has no BOM, and reading it via [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes + UTF-8 decode shows ± correctly encoded as \xc2\xb1. The text around it (±5 message window around the) is intact and meaningful.
The captured request-dump JSON is clean. Reading the dump file (request_dump_*.json) written by Hermes's own debug logging, parsing it with ConvertFrom-Json, and replaying the exact same request.body (model, messages, tools, extra_body — all four keys, unchanged) directly against https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions with a valid key succeeds (HTTP 200, normal completion). So whatever Hermes is actually putting on the wire is not what's in the dump file.
Not a tool-schema validation issue. All tool schemas (including delegate_task's nested tasks[].properties) are valid JSON Schema; replaying them works fine.
Not a third-party HTTP/JSON library bug. In the project's own venv:


python  import httpx, json
  s = 'session_search desc with \u00b15 message window'
  json.dumps({'description': s})  # -> {"description": "session_search desc with \u00b15 message window"} — correct

httpx 0.28.1, openai 2.24.0, requests 2.33.0 — all current, all behave correctly when given the clean string directly.


Not the _strip_non_ascii / _sanitize_tools_non_ascii sanitization pass. Those are last-resort ASCII-only fallbacks gated behind a specific retry branch in conversation_loop.py (~line 2199-2214) and would strip ± to nothing rather than produce an invalid code point. They're also not on the normal first-request path.
Not Windows console code page (chcp 936 / GB2312 default encoding). Confirmed python -c "import sys; print(sys.stdout.encoding, sys.getdefaultencoding())" → utf-8 utf-8 inside the venv. Replaying the dumped body from PowerShell (which goes through its own UTF-8 file read) succeeds regardless of the active code page, which somewhat argues against — but doesn't fully rule out — a console/locale encoding path being involved somewhere in the actual send path Hermes uses (vs. the debug-dump path).


Where I think the bug lives

The debug-dump writer and the actual outbound HTTP call apparently do not share the same serialized payload. The dump is clean; the live request is not. That points at either:


A second, separate serialization of tools happening specifically on the send path (not the dump path) that reintroduces corruption — possibly something dealing with encoding for a specific provider client construction in agent/auxiliary_client.py (there are 15+ separate OpenAI(...) construction sites and many separate client.chat.completions.create(**kwargs) call sites — worth checking whether any of them re-encode/re-decode kwargs["tools"] or pass it through something that isn't UTF-8-safe end to end), or
A timing/mutation issue where the in-memory tools list is mutated between when the dump is written and when the real request is sent (e.g., if dump-writing happens before some other in-place transform).


I wasn't able to go further without instrumenting the actual outbound chat.completions.create(**kwargs) call (e.g., temporarily logging repr(kwargs["tools"][9]["function"]["description"]) and the raw bytes right before the HTTP call fires) — that would conclusively show whether the corruption happens before or during serialization on the live path.

Possibly related

There's an open issue, "[Bug] StepFun API: Unterminated string error caused by broken JSON in context_compressor", which also describes a provider rejecting a malformed JSON request body — in that case an unterminated string originating from context_compressor, on the StepFun provider. The failure mode and code path are different (compressed conversation history vs. a static tool description; unterminated string vs. invalid Unicode code point), so I don't believe it's a duplicate of this report. But the pattern — JSON payloads becoming malformed somewhere between in-memory construction and the wire, surfacing only as a provider-side parse error — looks similar enough that the two might share an upstream cause (e.g. a shared serialization helper, or a shared code path that re-encodes/truncates strings before the final chat.completions.create() call). Flagging in case it helps maintainers spot a broader pattern across the request-construction pipeline.

### Steps to Reproduce

1.Enable the default toolset that includes session_search (default config — no special setup needed).
2.Send any message (你好 or otherwise — reproduces with plain ASCII content too) with 3.model: minimax/minimax-m3 via OpenRouter, or model: deepseek-v4-pro via DeepSeek direct.
Observe non-retryable HTTP 400 on the first attempt, every time.
Optional deeper repro (to confirm root cause, not required to see the bug):
4. Find the request-dump file Hermes writes on failure (%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\sessions\request_dump_*.json).
5. Parse it with ConvertFrom-Json in PowerShell and replay request.body directly against the provider's /chat/completions endpoint with a valid API key.
6. Observe that the replay succeeds — proving the dumped JSON is clean and the corruption happens only on Hermes's live send path.

### Expected Behavior

The request should be sent with valid, well-formed UTF-8 throughout tools[].function.description, and the provider should accept it (as confirmed by replaying the exact same dumped payload successfully). With session_search enabled, every request should succeed like it does with session_search disabled.

### Actual Behavior

Every request fails immediately with a non-retryable HTTP 400. DeepSeek's parser reports the precise cause:

Failed to parse the request body as JSON: tools[9].function.description: invalid unicode code point at line 489 column 2842

(Position shifts with overall payload size on repeat reproduction — e.g. line 516 column 3713 on a longer request — but the failing field is consistently tools[9].function.description, i.e. the session_search tool.) OpenRouter fails the same way but with a bare Error code: 400 and no body detail. The error is non-retryable and aborts the whole turn.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/L8PxOAppData\Local\hermes\sessions\request_dump_20260623_003844_eabf10_20
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/PlgJpvertFrom-Json
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/usBMS
```

### Operating System

Windows 10

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.17.0

```shell

```

### Proposed Fix (optional)

items.title: Photon sidecar hides delivery failure classes behind generic 500s
items.body:
## Problem

When the Photon sidecar catches send handler failures, it currently returns a generic 500 body such as:

```json
{"ok":false,"error":"internal sidecar error"}
```

The gateway adapter then cannot distinguish permanent auth/config failures from transient upstream failures. That makes logs less actionable and can cause the retry path to treat auth failures like transport failures.

## Expected

The sidecar should still avoid leaking raw stack traces, but it should return a small safe error class, including whether the failure is retryable. The Python adapter should preserve that retryability when producing `SendResult` values.

## Notes

Observed locally while diagnosing Photon delivery failures after sidecar restart. No credentials, message contents, or private account data are included here.

items.title: Slack: multiple agents in one channel all reply to every thread message (reply storms)
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

When several Hermes agents share a Slack channel, Hermes' thread auto-follow (once a bot is @-mentioned in a thread it follows every later message — `_mentioned_threads` in `plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py`) makes **every** bot open a turn on **every** subsequent thread message. An LLM that opens a turn must emit *something*, so the bots that weren't addressed reply with noise like "this isn't for me, staying out." With 2–3 bots in a channel, every plain follow-up turns into a pile-up ("reply storm") and burns tokens on turns that should never have run.

There's no built-in way to say "only the bot being talked to should answer this thread."

### Proposed Solution

A small `pre_gateway_dispatch` plugin that gates the turn **before the model runs**, using the rule **"the most-recently @-mentioned bot owns the thread"**:

- Message @-mentions me → I reply; the **last** mention in the message becomes the thread owner.
- Message @-mentions other bots but not me → I skip (`{"action": "skip"}`).
- Plain follow-up (no @) → only the current owner replies.
- DMs / top-level messages → unaffected (Slack's own root @-gating handles those).

Fully local: every bot following the thread sees every message and derives the same owner from the mention list, so they converge with **zero coordination** — no lock service, no shared state, no roster. A bot only needs its own Slack user id (one cached `auth.test`). Opt-in via `plugins.enabled`, no operator knobs.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Config-based topic/allowlist routing** (cf. #5756 Telegram `group_topics`, #9731 Mattermost sticky routing): per-channel config, platform-specific, and needs a maintained roster. Mention-ownership needs neither.
- **A central lock service** (bots claim/renew a lease over HTTP): works, but adds a network dependency and a single point of failure for what is really a pure function of the message text.
- **Letting the LLM decide "is this for me?"**: burns a full turn (and tokens) just to stay silent, and is unreliable.

### Feature Type

Plugin / integration (Slack platform).

### Scope

Small — one self-contained opt-in plugin (~200 LoC + 21 tests), no changes to core.

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR — **implemented in #50969**.

items.title: fix(photon): check_requirements() silently returns False after sidecar npm install fails.
items.body:
## Descrição

`check_requirements()` em `plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py` retorna `False` sem emitir nenhuma mensagem de log diagnóstica quando o sidecar do Photon não está disponível. Isso ocorre especificamente quando o `npm install` falha e `node_modules/` fica ausente (ou parcialmente criado), mas o operador que lê os logs do gateway vê apenas um aviso genérico do registry — sem indicação de **qual** condição falhou nem **por quê**.

---

## Causa Raiz

`check_requirements()` (`adapter.py:122-133`) é uma verificação de estado puro de filesystem. As três ramificações `return False` (linhas 125, 127, 132) são completamente silenciosas — nenhuma emite `logger.warning()` ou `logger.debug()` antes de retornar.

```python
def check_requirements() -> bool:
    """Return True when both Python deps and the Node sidecar are available."""
    if not HTTPX_AVAILABLE:
        return False           # ← silencioso
    if not shutil.which(os.getenv("PHOTON_NODE_BIN") or "node"):
        return False           # ← silencioso
    if not (_SIDECAR_DIR / "node_modules").exists():
        return False           # ← silencioso  ← principal ponto de falha pós-npm
    return True
```

Quando `npm install` falha (`_install_sidecar()`, `cli.py:397-398`), o output do npm vai direto ao terminal via `subprocess.run(..., check=False)` sem `capture_output=True` — e é perdido. Uma chamada subsequente a `check_requirements()` (no start do gateway ou `hermes status`) não tem como recuperar esse erro.

---

## Fluxo completo do problema

```
_cmd_setup (cli.py:268-271)
  └─ _install_sidecar() (cli.py:368-399)
       ├─ subprocess.run([npm, "ci"],  check=False)   ← sem capture_output
       │    returncode != 0 → fallback
       └─ subprocess.run([npm, "install"], check=False) ← sem capture_output
            returncode != 0 → print("npm install failed", stderr)
            retorna proc.returncode (não-zero)
  ← rc != 0 → _cmd_setup retorna cedo
  → node_modules NUNCA é criado

[gateway start / hermes status / create_adapter()]
  └─ check_fn() = check_requirements()
       └─ (_SIDECAR_DIR / "node_modules").exists() → False
            return False   ← linha 132, sem log
  └─ registry.py:221-228 → logger.warning("requirements not met (Run: hermes photon setup...)")
       ← mensagem genérica, não diz qual das 3 condições disparou
```

---

## Quatro Riscos Identificados

### Risco 1 — Falha silenciosa no gateway (alto)
`create_adapter()` em `platform_registry.py:221-228` retorna `None` quando `check_fn()` → `False`, logando apenas a hint genérica. O canal iMessage fica mudo sem nenhum alerta acionável para o operador.

### Risco 2 — `node_modules/` parcial passa o guard (alto)
Se o `npm install` falha no meio (timeout de rede, ENOSPC, EACCES), o npm pode ter criado `node_modules/` antes de abortar. O check `.exists()` retorna `True` — `check_requirements()` passa, o adapter é instanciado, e o sidecar crasha em runtime com erro de módulo não encontrado. Mais difícil de diagnosticar do que um `False` limpo.

### Risco 3 — Output do npm descartado (médio)
`_install_sidecar()` usa `subprocess.run` sem `capture_output`, `stdout=PIPE` ou `stderr=PIPE`. O erro real do npm (versão incompatível, timeout de rede, lockfile drift) existe apenas no terminal no momento do setup e nunca é armazenado ou re-surfaceado.

### Risco 4 — Três condições indistinguíveis (baixo)
As três ramificações `return False` (httpx ausente, node não encontrado, node_modules ausente) produzem o mesmo zero-log externamente. O operador não consegue distinguir se precisa de `pip install httpx`, instalar Node.js, ou reexecutar `hermes photon setup`.

---

## Testes que Comprovam os Riscos

Arquivo: `tests/plugins/platforms/photon/test_check_requirements_risks.py`

| Teste | O que prova |
|---|---|
| `test_risk1_missing_node_modules_returns_false_with_no_log` | `caplog.records == []` — zero logs emitidos pela função ao retornar False |
| `test_risk2_empty_node_modules_passes_guard` | `check_requirements()` retorna `True` com `node_modules/` vazio (falso positivo real) |
| `test_risk3_install_sidecar_subprocess_calls_have_no_output_capture` | Inspeção AST do source real: nenhum `subprocess.run` tem `capture_output`/PIPE |
| `test_risk4_all_false_conditions_produce_no_log[*]` | Todos os 3 cenários False produzem `caplog.records == []` |

Os testes **passam** com o código atual (provando que os riscos existem) e vão **falhar** após o fix ser aplicado — comportamento correto de testes de regressão de bug.

---

## Fix Proposto (KISS — 3 warnings adicionados)

Adicionar `logger.warning()` nas três ramificações silenciosas em `adapter.py:122-133`:

```python
def check_requirements() -> bool:
    """Return True when both Python deps and the Node sidecar are available."""
    if not HTTPX_AVAILABLE:
        logger.warning("photon: httpx not installed — pip install httpx")
        return False
    if not shutil.which(os.getenv("PHOTON_NODE_BIN") or "node"):
        logger.warning(
            "photon: node binary '%s' not found on PATH",
            os.getenv("PHOTON_NODE_BIN") or "node",
        )
        return False
    if not (_SIDECAR_DIR / "node_modules").exists():
        logger.warning(
            "photon: sidecar node_modules missing at %s — run: hermes photon setup",
            _SIDECAR_DIR,
        )
        return False
    return True
```

**Checklist de risco do patch:**
- [x] Assinatura `() -> bool` inalterada — registry e gateway não quebram
- [x] Zero novos imports — `logger` já existe no módulo (`logging.getLogger(__name__)`)
- [x] Zero side-effects novos — `logger.warning` é read-only
- [x] Valor de retorno inalterado — `test_check_requirements_without_node` continua passando
- [x] Fluxo de credenciais/perfis intacto — patch não toca em auth
- [x] Invariantes de caching e deduplicação preservados

---

## Arquivos Afetados

- `plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py` — linhas 122-133 (fix)
- `tests/plugins/platforms/photon/test_check_requirements_risks.py` (testes novos)

items.body:
## Orphaned `_keep_typing` asyncio task persists `sendChatAction` after agent cache idle-eviction

### Description
The Telegram typing indicator persists indefinitely after an agent session is evicted from cache due to idle TTL. The `_keep_typing` background task becomes orphaned and continues firing `sendChatAction` every ~2 seconds with nothing to cancel it.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Exchange messages with Hermes in a Telegram forum topic
2. Wait for agent to be idle long enough to trigger cache idle-TTL eviction (~1 hour default)
3. Observe the typing indicator persists in the topic indefinitely after eviction
4. New messages to the same topic spin up a fresh agent, but the orphaned task remains

### Log Evidence
```
2026-06-22 11:00:01 — Last response sent (27 chars)
2026-06-22 12:00:32 — Agent cache idle-TTL evict (idle=3631s, 1 agent evicted)
2026-06-22 14:44:19 — User notices typing indicator still active
```
No gateway events occurred between 12:00 and 14:44 — only the orphaned typing task was running.

### Root Cause
In `gateway/platforms/base.py`, the `_keep_typing` task runs as an `asyncio.Task` inside `_process_message_background`. Normally a `finally` block cancels it via `_stop_typing_refresh`. This works.

The bug is in the cache eviction path (`gateway/run.py`, `_sweep_idle_cached_agents`, L~13349):
1. The agent entry is popped from `_agent_cache`
2. `_release_evicted_agent_soft()` is called on a **daemon thread**
3. This calls `agent.release_clients()` — frees HTTP connections only
4. It does NOT interact with the asyncio event loop where the `_keep_typing` task lives

`_keep_typing`'s `stop_event` comes from `_active_sessions` (L4162) which persists across evictions. If the old task is still alive when a new session starts, the new session reuses the same event — creating ambiguity about which task owns the stop signal.

### Relevant Code
| File | Lines | What |
|------|-------|------|
| `gateway/platforms/base.py` | 4174-4179 | typing task creation |
| `gateway/platforms/base.py` | 3139-3204 | `_keep_typing` loop |
| `gateway/platforms/base.py` | 4561-4565 | `finally` block (normal stop) |
| `gateway/run.py` | 13349-13384 | idle sweep (no typing cancellation) |
| `gateway/run.py` | 13244-13253 | `_release_evicted_agent_soft` (daemon thread) |

### Workaround
Restarting the gateway kills all orphaned tasks. Extending `gateway.agent_cache_idle_ttl_secs` reduces the race window.

### Environment
- Hermes: git install, running ~5 days
- Platform: Telegram forum topic
- OS: Linux 6.17.0-22-generic

items.body:
# BUG: Windows pip upgrade fails with os error 32 (hermes.exe locked by self)

## 描述

Windows 上 `uv pip install --upgrade hermes-agent`（或 Hermes Desktop 右下角点更新）失败：

```
error: failed to remove file `...\Scripts\hermes.exe`: 另一个程序正在使用此文件，进程无法访问。 (os error 32)
```

## 原因

hermes.exe 被当前运行的 Hermes 进程锁住，Windows 不允许覆盖正在运行的可执行文件。Linux/macOS 无此问题（inode 替换机制）。

## 复现步骤

1. 运行 Hermes Desktop 或 Hermes CLI
2. 在桌面点更新，或终端执行 `uv pip install --upgrade hermes-agent`
3. 报 os error 32

## 建议修复方案

1. **自身进程退出后再升级** — 下载新版到临时位置，启动一个 .bat 脚本等待父进程退出后替换 exe 再重启
2. **延迟替换** — 下载到缓存，下次启动时执行替换（类似浏览器更新策略）
3. **提供 Windows 独立安装包 (.exe/.msi)** — 绕过 pip venv 的文件锁问题,提醒用户需完全关闭Hermes Desktop再开始安装

## 环境

- Windows 10
- Python 3.12.8
- Hermes v0.16.0 (pip install)
- Hermes Desktop (Electron GUI)

items.title: [Bug]: Slack gateway evicts arbitrary thread timestamps from _bot_message_ts / _mentioned_threads — bot silently stops responding to active threads
items.body:
## Description

In `gateway/platforms/slack.py`, two `set` objects (`_bot_message_ts` and `_mentioned_threads`) have cap-based eviction logic that uses `list(set)[:N]` to select entries to remove. However, **Python sets have no guaranteed iteration order**, so this removes arbitrary entries — not the oldest ones as intended.

## Impact

`_bot_message_ts` is checked on every incoming thread reply to decide if the bot should respond (line ~2350: `event_thread_ts in self._bot_message_ts`). When the cap is hit and a recently-active thread's timestamp is evicted by chance, the bot **silently stops responding** to that thread. The same applies to `_mentioned_threads` for mention-based routing.

This is silent data loss: no error is logged, the bot simply ignores messages in affected threads.

## Reproduction

Run a busy Slack workspace with >5000 bot-participated threads. After the cap is hit, observe that some active threads receive no bot responses even when directly addressed.

## Root Cause

Three locations in `slack.py`:

```python
# ~line 822 (send)
for old_ts in list(self._bot_message_ts)[:excess]:   # ← unordered
    self._bot_message_ts.discard(old_ts)

# ~line 1153 (_record_uploaded_file_thread)
for old_ts in list(self._bot_message_ts)[:excess]:   # ← unordered
    self._bot_message_ts.discard(old_ts)

# ~line 2007 (_handle_slack_message)
to_remove = list(self._mentioned_threads)[:self._MENTIONED_THREADS_MAX // 2]  # ← unordered
```

## Fix

Replace `list(...)` with `sorted(...)`. Slack timestamps are `"unix_seconds.seq_num"` (e.g. `"1718234567.123456"`), so lexicographic sort = chronological sort, and the oldest entries are correctly evicted first.

### Bug Description

## Bug: Cron Jobs Never Fire Despite Ticker Being Alive

### Description
Cron jobs are scheduled and show as "scheduled" in `hermes cron list`, but never execute or deliver to Telegram, even after multiple gateway restarts and hermes updates.

### Environment
- **Hermes Agent:** v0.17.0 (2026.6.19, commit 2a58fee1a)
- **OS:** Linux (6.8.0-71-generic)
- **Python:** 3.11.15
- **Deployment:** User-level systemd service
- **Platform:** Telegram

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a cron job: `hermes cron create --deliver origin --prompt "test message" --schedule "2026-06-22T20:07:00"`
2. Wait for the scheduled time
3. Job does not fire or deliver to Telegram

### Expected Behavior
Cron job should execute at the scheduled time and deliver output to the origin chat (Telegram).

### Actual Behavior
- Job remains in "scheduled" state indefinitely
- `hermes cron status` shows ticker is alive (heartbeat updates every 60s)
- No job execution occurs
- No error logs appear in gateway.log
- No delivery to Telegram

### Key Details
- **Job origin data is correct:** `{"platform": "telegram", "chat_id": "70735323", "thread_id": null}`
- **Deliver setting:** `deliver: "origin"` (verified in jobs.json)
- **Multiple restarts attempted:** Gateway restarted 3+ times, `hermes update` run twice
- **Latest fix applied:** Pulled latest main branch (commit 2a58fee1a from 2026-06-22) which includes PR #50016 (cron ticker fixes)
- **Heartbeat present:** `hermes cron status` shows "Ticker heartbeat: 43s ago" — ticker thread is alive but not executing jobs

### Logs & Debug Info
- No cron scheduler logs appear even with `logging.level: debug` set in config.yaml
- Gateway logs show no tick activity or delivery attempts
- `hermes cron status` output:
  
  ✓ Gateway is running — cron jobs will fire automatically
    PID: 4580
    Ticker heartbeat: 43s ago
    9 active job(s)
    Next run: 2026-06-23T07:00:00+00:00


### Related Issues
- Possibly related to #32895 (cron ticker thread stops silently) — but that fix is supposedly applied
- Possibly related to #36734 (get_fallback_chain NameError) — but that fix is also applied

### Attempted Workarounds
- Restarted gateway multiple times
- Ran `hermes update`
- Rebuilt hermes-agent from latest main branch
- Set `logging.level: debug` in config.yaml
- Created jobs with explicit UTC times

### Question
Is there a known issue preventing `deliver=origin` jobs from reaching the Telegram platform adapter? Is the adapter being passed correctly to the cron scheduler in the current main branch?


### Steps to Reproduce

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure Hermes Gateway is running with Telegram configured:
   
2. Create a test cron job scheduled for 2 minutes in the future (replace FUTURE_TIME with actual UTC time 2 minutes from now):
   
 hermes cron create \
     --name "test-cron-delivery" \
     --prompt "test message" \
     --schedule "FUTURE_TIME" \
     --deliver "origin"
    Example: If current time is 2026-06-22 20:00:00 UTC, use:
hermes cron create \
     --name "test-cron-delivery" \
     --prompt "test message" \
     --schedule "2026-06-22T20:02:00" \
     --deliver "origin"

3. Verify job was created:
   
   hermes cron list | grep test-cron-delivery
   

4. Wait for scheduled time to pass (2 minutes)

5. Check if message was delivered to your Telegram chat (it will not be)

6. Verify job is still in "scheduled" state:
   
   hermes cron list | grep test-cron-delivery
   

7. Check gateway logs for any cron activity:
   
   tail -100 ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log | grep -i "cron\|deliver"
   
   Result: No cron-related logs appear

8. Check ticker status:
   
   hermes cron status
   
   Result: Ticker shows as alive but no jobs fire
   



### Expected Behavior

## Expected Behavior

1. At the scheduled time (2026-06-22T20:02:00 UTC), the cron ticker should:
   - Detect that the job is due via `get_due_jobs()`
   - Call `run_one_job()` to execute the job
   - Generate output from the agent

2. The output should be delivered to Telegram:
   - `_deliver_result()` should resolve the delivery target using the job's origin data
   - The message should be sent via the Telegram adapter
   - User receives the message in their Telegram chat (70735323)

3. Job state should update:

   - `last_status` should show "completed"
   - Job should transition from "scheduled" to appropriate final state

4. Logs should show execution:

   - Delivery attempt should be logged


### Actual Behavior

## Actual Behavior

1. At the scheduled time (2026-06-22T20:02:00 UTC):
   - The cron ticker does NOT detect the due job
   - `run_one_job()` is never called
   - No agent execution occurs

2. Telegram receives nothing:
   - No message is sent to the user's Telegram chat
   - No delivery attempt is logged
   - User sees no indication the job ran

3. Job state remains unchanged:
   - `last_run_at` remains null
   - `last_status` remains null

   - `next_run_at` does not update

4. No logs appear:
   - `hermes cron status` shows ticker is alive (heartbeat updates every 60s)
   - Gateway logs show NO cron tick activity, no job execution, no delivery attempts
   - Even with `logging.level: debug` in config.yaml, no cron scheduler logs appear
   - Silent failure — no error messages, no warnings, nothing

5. Contradictory status:

items.title: Multiplexer: secondary profile's platform token leaks from the default profile (_apply_env_overrides uses os.getenv, not the profile secret scope)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

When `gateway.multiplex_profiles` is on, a **secondary** profile's platform adapter is configured with the **default** profile's bot token instead of its own. For Telegram this means the secondary profile's adapter polls the *default* bot's token — producing a perpetual `getUpdates` 409 *"Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request"* on the default token, while the secondary profile's own bot is never polled and stays completely silent.

Root cause: `gateway/config.py::_apply_env_overrides` resolves platform tokens with raw `os.getenv(...)`, bypassing the per-profile secret scope that the multiplexer installs — even though that scope's own docstring promises it is the authoritative credential source.

**Version:** hermes 0.17.0 (NixOS module, container mode / rootful podman, two Telegram profiles `default` + `family`).

## Repro

1. Create a second profile with its own Telegram bot token in its `.env`:
   ```
   hermes profile create family --clone
   # set a DIFFERENT TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN in ~/.hermes/profiles/family/.env
   ```
2. Enable multiplexing on the default profile (`multiplex_profiles: true` in the default `config.yaml`).
3. Start the (single, multiplexed) gateway and watch both bots.

**Expected:** the `family` adapter polls the `family` bot token; both bots respond.
**Actual:** the `family` adapter polls the **default** bot's token. The default token now has two concurrent `getUpdates` pollers → 409 conflict loop on the default bot; the `family` bot token is polled by nobody → the family bot never receives updates.

## Root cause

The multiplexer starts each secondary profile's adapters under `_profile_runtime_scope(profile_home)` (`gateway/run.py:1379`), which installs the profile's `.env` as the secret scope. Its docstring is explicit about the contract:

```python
# gateway/run.py:1386
#   2. ``set_secret_scope`` — installs the profile's ``.env`` secrets as the
#      authoritative credential source, so ``get_secret`` reads this profile's
#      keys and never the process-global ``os.environ`` (which in a
#      multiplexer may hold another profile's values).
```

But inside that scope, `_start_one_profile_adapters` calls `load_gateway_config()` → `_apply_env_overrides()`, which reads the token straight from the process-global environment, **not** through `get_secret`:

```python
# gateway/config.py:1232 (inside _apply_env_overrides, def at :1212)
    # Telegram
    telegram_token = os.getenv("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN")
    if telegram_token:
        telegram_config = _enable_from_env(Platform.TELEGRAM)
        telegram_config.token = telegram_token
```

`os.environ["TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN"]` holds the **default** profile's token (loaded at gateway boot via the default `.env`), so the family profile's `telegram_config.token` is overwritten with the default token regardless of the active secret scope.

This is **not** Telegram-specific — every platform token in `_apply_env_overrides` uses the same `os.getenv` pattern (`DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, `WHATSAPP_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `WEIXIN_TOKEN`, …), so any multiplexed second bot of any platform inherits the default profile's credential. `get_secret` (`agent/secret_scope.py:123`) is never called anywhere in `gateway/config.py`.

## Impact

- Multiplexing a second Telegram (or Discord/Slack/etc.) bot is effectively broken: the second bot is silent and the **default** bot is degraded by a 409 poll-conflict loop.
- Fails silently — see the companion issue: the same-token collision guard that should flag "two profiles polling the same token" is also blind to Telegram, so nothing is logged.

## Suggested fix

In `_apply_env_overrides`, resolve secrets through the scope-aware accessor the docstring already promises, e.g.:

```python
from agent.secret_scope import get_secret
telegram_token = get_secret("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN")   # honors the active profile scope, falls back to os.environ
```

applied consistently to all platform tokens (and arguably the other per-profile secrets) in that function. That restores the documented invariant ("`get_secret` reads this profile's keys and never the process-global `os.environ`") for the multiplexed inbound path while leaving single-profile gateways unchanged.

## Workaround

Don't multiplex. Run each extra profile as its own gateway process (`hermes -p <name> gateway run`). A separate process loads that profile's `.env` into its own `os.environ`, so the `os.getenv` read returns the correct token.

items.title: Multiplexer: same-token collision detection is dead for Telegram — _adapter_credential_fingerprint never finds a token at adapter.config.token
items.body:
## Summary

The multiplexer's same-token collision guard never fires for **Telegram** (and any adapter that stores its credential at `adapter.config.token` rather than as a direct attribute). `_adapter_credential_fingerprint` only probes a fixed list of *instance* attributes, none of which the Telegram adapter sets, so it returns `None` and conflict detection is silently skipped — exactly when two profiles end up polling the same bot token.

**Version:** hermes 0.17.0 (NixOS module, container mode, two Telegram profiles under `multiplex_profiles`).

## Root cause

`_adapter_credential_fingerprint` (`gateway/run.py:6996`) discovers the credential only via direct attributes on the adapter:

```python
# gateway/run.py:6996
@staticmethod
def _adapter_credential_fingerprint(adapter: Any) -> Optional[str]:
    token = None
    for attr in ("token", "bot_token", "_token", "api_token", "_bot_token"):
        val = getattr(adapter, attr, None)
        if isinstance(val, str) and val.strip():
            token = val.strip()
            break
    if not token:
        return None        # ← Telegram always lands here
    ...
```

The Telegram adapter sets **none** of those attributes. Its token lives at `self.config.token`:

```python
# plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py
2014:   if not self.config.token:
2019:   if not self._acquire_platform_lock('telegram-bot-token', self.config.token, 'Telegram bot token'):
2023:   builder = Application.builder().token(self.config.token)
```

So `_adapter_credential_fingerprint` returns `None` for every Telegram adapter, and both call sites skip the check on `fp is not None`:

- `_start_secondary_profile_adapters` (`gateway/run.py:6876`) seeds `claimed` from the active profile's adapters — Telegram contributes nothing.
- `_start_one_profile_adapters` (`gateway/run.py:6943`) looks up `claimed.get((platform, fp))` — `fp` is `None`, so the duplicate-poll branch is never entered and no error is logged.

The guard's purpose, per its own docstring, is "to detect two profiles claiming the same bot token" — which is precisely the failure produced by the companion issue (per-profile token leak), so the one safety net that should have surfaced that bug is itself inert. Note the comment at `gateway/run.py:7030` already acknowledges the token can come from `PlatformConfig.token`, yet the probe doesn't look there.

## Impact

- No "two profiles configure telegram with the same credential — refusing to start the duplicate" error is ever emitted for Telegram, even when it's true.
- Combined with the token-leak issue, a misconfigured/buggy multiplex setup degrades silently instead of failing loud.

## Suggested fix

Also probe `adapter.config.token` (the canonical location for plugin adapters) in `_adapter_credential_fingerprint`, e.g. after the direct-attribute loop:

```python
if not token:
    cfg = getattr(adapter, "config", None)
    cfg_token = getattr(cfg, "token", None)
    if isinstance(cfg_token, str) and cfg_token.strip():
        token = cfg_token.strip()
```

That makes the collision detector effective for Telegram (and any other adapter following the `config.token` convention).

items.title: Desktop app shows legacy profile-local cron jobs after root cron store migration

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

After the cron storage migration introduced for shared root-level cron jobs (#32091), `hermes cron list` and the scheduler read the new root store, but the Desktop app can still display the old profile-local `jobs.json`. This makes jobs appear active in the UI even though the CLI/scheduler does not see or run them.

## Observed behavior

On Windows, with active profile `dominika`:

- Desktop app showed 3 active cron jobs from:
  `C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\profiles\dominika\cron\jobs.json`
- `hermes cron list` returned:
  `No scheduled jobs.`
- Python inspection confirmed the active cron module now uses:
  `C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\cron\jobs.json`
- That root `jobs.json` did not exist, while the profile-local legacy file existed and contained jobs.

The CLI also printed this warning when importing/listing jobs:

```text
Cron jobs now live at C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\cron\jobs.json (shared across profiles). A legacy profile-local store exists at C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\profiles\dominika\cron\jobs.json and is no longer read; re-create those jobs or move them into the root store. (#32091)
```

## Expected behavior

One of these should happen automatically:

1. Desktop app should read the same root cron store as CLI/scheduler, or
2. Desktop app should show a migration warning instead of showing stale legacy jobs as active, or
3. Hermes should migrate legacy profile-local cron jobs into the root store on startup/update.

## Why this is dangerous

The UI made it look like scheduled jobs were active, but the scheduler/CLI did not see them. This can silently disable watchdogs, update watchers, reminders, or other important automations after an update/migration.

## Reproduction / Diagnostics

Environment:

```text
Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (2026.6.19) · upstream 2a58fee1
Project: C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent
Windows profile path: C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\profiles\dominika
```

Commands/results:

```bash
hermes --version
hermes cron list
```

`hermes cron list` returned no jobs.

Direct inspection:

```python
from cron.jobs import JOBS_FILE, list_jobs
print(JOBS_FILE)
print(JOBS_FILE.exists())
print(len(list_jobs(include_disabled=True)))
```

Output:

```text
C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\cron\jobs.json
False
0
```

But legacy file existed and contained jobs:

```text
C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\profiles\dominika\cron\jobs.json
```

## Workaround used

Manually copied/merged the jobs from:

```text
C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\profiles\dominika\cron\jobs.json
```

into:

```text
C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\hermes\cron\jobs.json
```

After that, `hermes cron list` correctly showed the jobs again.

`list_windows` returns 0 windows despite multiple visible windows open (Firefox, Obsidian, Telegram, etc.).

System Python pyatspi works correctly:

import pyatspi

items.title: Feature: /resume-last slash command to resume most recent session in one step

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Proposal

Add a `/resume-last` (alias `/rl`) slash command that instantly resumes the most recent session without requiring the user to look up a session ID or title.

## Current behavior

To resume a previous session, the user must:
1. Run `/sessions` or `/history` to list sessions
2. Find the session ID or title
3. Run `/resume <id_or_title>`

This is 3 steps for a very common action — getting back to the last conversation.

## Proposed behavior

`/resume-last` (or `/rl`) finds the most recent session (excluding the current one) and delegates to the existing `/resume` logic. One keystroke.

```
> /resume-last
↻ Resumed session "Debugging OpenClaw" (47 messages). Conversation restored.
```

Works in both CLI and gateway (Telegram, Discord, etc.).

## Implementation

- Finds the most recent session via `_list_recent_sessions(limit=1)` (CLI) or `_session_db.list_sessions_rich(limit=10)` filtered by source (gateway)
- Delegates to `_handle_resume_command` so all existing resume logic (compression-chain resolution, session switching, history recap, memory-provider notification) is reused unchanged
- No new infrastructure — just a thin wrapper around existing `/resume`

items.title: Discord: single user message dispatched twice → 2 agent runs / 2 responses (v0.17.0)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

A single Discord message from a user is dispatched twice into `_handle_message_with_agent`, producing two independent agent runs and two responses. Reproducible on the latest `main` (commit `e9b86f352fc73db5ca3de6e3fb50ef57d774f8f9`, v0.17.0), single-profile single-adapter setup, with text batching disabled and history backfill disabled.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.17.0** (2026.6.19), commit `e9b86f352`
- Python 3.13.5, OpenAI SDK 2.24.0
- Docker (Linux container, `nikolaik/python-nodejs` base via image build)
- Single profile (default), `multiplex_profiles: false`, one Discord bot, single Hermes process

Relevant config:
```yaml
discord:
  history_backfill: false
  reply_to_mode: 'off'
  require_mention: false
  ignore_no_mention: false
```
Relevant env:
```
HERMES_DISCORD_TEXT_BATCH_DELAY_SECONDS=0
DISCORD_REPLY_TO_MODE=off
DISCORD_HISTORY_BACKFILL=false
```

## Repro

User sends a single `ping` in a Discord channel. Bot responds with 2 (sometimes 3) separate Discord messages, each containing the agent's reply, each rendered with a reply-quote chain back to the user's original message despite `reply_to_mode: off`.

## Log evidence (clean upstream, no patches)

```
21:23:45,838 INFO hermes_plugins.discord_platform.adapter: [Discord] Flushing text batch agent:main:discord:group:<chat>:<user> (4 chars)
21:23:46,206 INFO gateway.run: inbound message: platform=discord user=Mark chat=<chat> msg='ping' reply_to_id=None reply_to_text=''
21:23:46,641 INFO gateway.run: inbound message: platform=discord user=Mark chat=<chat> msg='ping'
21:23:49,620 INFO gateway.run: response ready: platform=discord chat=<chat> time=3.0s api_calls=1 response=4 chars
21:23:49,642 INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Discord] Sending response (4 chars) to <chat>
21:23:53,868 INFO gateway.run: response ready: platform=discord chat=<chat> time=7.7s api_calls=1 response=4 chars
21:23:53,902 INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Discord] Sending response (4 chars) to <chat>
```

Observations:
1. Discord's `on_message` fires once (single `Flushing text batch` line, batching disabled but the log still appears once).
2. Two `inbound message` log lines fire ~435ms apart.
3. **Curious anomaly:** the second `inbound message` log lacks the `reply_to_id=...` / `reply_to_text=...` suffix even though `gateway/run.py:8843` is the only `logger.info("inbound message:...")` call site in the entire codebase, and that format unconditionally appends those fields. Suggests the second invocation may be reaching that log line via a code path that doesn't construct the same event (older event copy?), OR there is a second log site I cannot grep.
4. Both `_handle_message_with_agent` invocations complete a full agent turn and trigger `_send_with_retry` → 2 `Sending response` events → user sees 2+ bot replies.

Despite `reply_to_mode='off'` (verified at adapter init: `DBG_REPLY_MODE init='off' env='off' cfg_val='off' cfg_type=PlatformConfig`), the Discord client renders each reply with the inline reply-reference UI quoting the user's message.

## What I've ruled out

- Multi-process: only one `hermes gateway run` Python process running (confirmed via `ps`).
- `multiplex_profiles`: `False` (default).
- `history_backfill`: disabled; first message at 21:23:46 is the user's live ping, not a replayed backfill.
- Text batching duplicate-fire: `HERMES_DISCORD_TEXT_BATCH_DELAY_SECONDS=0` → batching disabled.
- Clawdbot / second bot token: separate Hermes bot token, exclusively connected to one Discord application.
- discord.py reconnect zombie clients: only one client instance in adapter, single `Connected as Richard#3238` line after each restart.

## Related issues

- #44497 (WeChat duplicate response from one user message) — similar symptom on a different adapter
- #25349 (Discord streaming duplicates final response) — likely related but streaming is disabled here
- #43835 (Telegram double messages, CLOSED) — symptomatically similar
- #16108 (umbrella idempotency request)

## What would help me file this confidently

- Is there a code path I'm missing that calls `_handle_message_with_agent` outside of `_handle_message` line 8412? (Grep finds only this one call site in production code.)
- Is there a known interaction between Hermes' `_AGENT_PENDING_SENTINEL` race guard and a fast follow-up dispatch on Discord?
- Why does the second `inbound message` log line have a different format than the first when they should share a single format string?

Happy to attach the full session log, gateway log, or a strace if helpful.

items.title: Guidance request: user-owned, portable LLM memory across models/tools

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
This is not necessarily a bug report; it is a request for guidance/design direction around long-term memory architecture in Hermes.

I have been dealing with this problem for several years, and I still have not found a reliable way to solve it. The problem is that I want the memory of the LLM I talk to to be under my own control.

I talked to ChatGPT for several years, and it developed a relatively good understanding of me, but the quality of its models was weak at that time. Then Google released a better model, so I moved to Gemini on the web, and from the beginning I explained myself to it again: all the things that matter to me, my concerns, my projects, and my goals. It again developed a good understanding of me. Then Anthropic released a better model, and I moved there, and the same thing happened again.

Now I am using my own server so that I can use different models, have a shared tool, and switch between models whenever I want. But now this tool itself has become another challenge.

When I find a tool better and more effective than Hermes, I will have to manually move the memory to the new tool, if it supports it and if the migration process does not have problems, because Hermes puts different things in different places: `soul.md`, `memory.md`, `user.md`, and almost every task or project generally has its own dedicated skill.

On the other hand, Hermes keeps updating `memory.md` and changes things that I manually entered myself. Over time, to make room for new things that I want it to remember, it compresses the memory more and more, which causes the quality of previous memories to be lost, because this file has a character limit.

Honestly, I do not know what the best approach is.

An LLM wiki could be one way to put related information next to each other, but I still think that an effective memory should be a semantic database built on top of an LLM wiki. The main memory should be a database, and the wiki should be the reliable documents that add details to the memory.

For example, I may remember my national ID card number, but I may not remember the other information on my national ID card. When needed, I go and pick up the national ID card, look at it, and read the details from it.

LLM memory should have the same kind of structure. When you ask an LLM something, it should know what you are talking about, and without filling the context with useless data, it should go and find only the relevant data from the correct place, and fill the context that will be sent to the LLM only with that content.

What I would like guidance on:

1. Is there a recommended architecture in Hermes for making long-term memory user-owned, portable, and model/tool agnostic?
2. Should `USER.md` / `MEMORY.md` be treated only as short bootstrap hints and pointers, while detailed memory lives in user-owned documents or a semantic store?
3. Is there a supported way to prevent Hermes from rewriting or compressing manually curated memory entries?
4. Are there existing extension points for building a semantic/vector/graph memory layer over user-owned wiki-style documents, with provenance and retrieval into context only when relevant?
5. If this is not currently supported, what would be the cleanest path to experiment with it: a custom memory provider, a plugin, Mem0/Honcho integration, skills, or some other architecture?

I am looking for guidance on the intended direction rather than asking for an immediate implementation.

items.title: [Feature]: Desktop app should access HTTP API for management — hybrid architecture (WebSocket for chat + HTTP for admin)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

The Hermes Desktop app and the Web Dashboard have diverged significantly in capability. The dashboard exposes 18 management pages via HTTP API; the desktop has 9 views, most of which are chat-focused. This forces desktop users to switch to the browser for any non-chat management task.

### What the dashboard can do that the desktop cannot

| Area | Dashboard (HTTP) | Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin install/enable/remove/hub | ✅ Full lifecycle | ❌ Not available |
| Skills search/install/publish/taps/audit | ✅ Full lifecycle | ⚠️ Listing + toggle only |
| MCP server management | ✅ | ❌ |
| Runtime logs | ✅ | ❌ |
| Analytics/usage stats | ✅ | ❌ |
| Env vars + secrets management | ✅ | ❌ (hidden in settings) |
| Messaging channel config | ✅ | ❌ |
| Config editor with schema | ✅ Full | ⚠️ Partial |
| Webhook management | ✅ | ❌ |
| Dashboard themes/plugins | ✅ | ❌ |

### Root cause

The desktop communicates with the backend via **WebSocket + PTY bridge** (`tui_gateway`). This is correct for real-time chat (message deltas, tool progress, streaming) but the gateway does not expose management operations. The dashboard uses **HTTP API** (`web_server.py`) for management, which the desktop never connects to.

```
Dashboard:  Browser → HTTP → web_server.py → management
                         ↘ WebSocket → gateway → chat

Desktop:    Electron → WebSocket → gateway → chat
                           ↘ ❌ no management channel
```

## Proposed solution: hybrid architecture

Keep WebSocket for chat (it works well for bidirectional streaming). Add HTTP API access for management operations. This is not a rewrite — it is an additive change.

```
Desktop (proposed):
  Chat ←→ WebSocket ←→ Gateway          (unchanged)
  Management ←→ HTTP ←→ web_server.py   (new)
```

### Implementation options (not mutually exclusive)

**Option A — Plugin loader (already in progress)**
PR [#46466](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/46466) brings the dashboard plugin system into Electron. Dashboard plugins (kanban, achievements, future skills hub) render natively. This covers the plugin ecosystem but not standalone management pages.

**Option B — HTTP client module in desktop**
Add an HTTP client to the Electron app that speaks directly to `/api/...` endpoints. Expose it via `window.hermesDesktop` IPC or a dedicated module. Reuse or adapt existing dashboard pages (`SkillsPage`, `PluginsPage`, etc.) as desktop views.

**Option C — Gateway management endpoints**
Extend `tui_gateway` to proxy management operations. Clean architecturally but requires changes to the critical gateway path.

### Recommended approach

Start with **A** (plugin loader — already has PR), then **B** (HTTP client for remaining management). C is a longer-term option if the team wants a single protocol.

## Related issues and PRs

| Item | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [#49363](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/49363) | Desktop load dashboard plugins |
| [#46466](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/46466) | PR: plugin loader (kanban + achievements) |
| [#41222](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/41222) | Kanban in desktop |
| [#41756](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/41756) | PR: kanban panel |
| [#13453](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/13453) | Skills Hub Web UI enhancement |
| [#50173](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/50173) | Kanban panel (duplicate, consolidated) |

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is the hybrid approach (WebSocket chat + HTTP management) aligned with the desktop direction?
2. Should management views reuse dashboard components directly, or be rewritten as desktop-native views?
3. Is there a preferred ordering — plugin loader first, then HTTP client? Or a different phrasing?
4. Are there security considerations for the desktop making direct HTTP calls to `web_server.py` (session tokens, CORS, etc.)?

items.title: [Feature]: Support utilizing project .mcp.json MCP server configs

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

I'm trying to use Hermes in a workflow where MCP servers are already defined in a project-local `.mcp.json` file, but Hermes currently only reads MCP servers from its own config file (`config.yaml` via `hermes mcp add/list/remove/test`).

This means the same MCP server has to be configured separately for Hermes and for other MCP-capable tools/editors. For example, in an Unreal Engine project, the project may already contain a `.mcp.json` entry for an Unreal MCP endpoint, but Hermes still needs a separate `hermes mcp add unreal-mcp --url ...` entry before it can expose those tools.

The result is duplicated config, extra setup steps, and confusion about why an MCP server works in one tool but not in Hermes.

### Proposed Solution

Add first-class support for utilizing MCP server definitions from project-local `.mcp.json` files, without requiring users to duplicate or import them into Hermes' global config.

Hermes could discover `.mcp.json` in the current workspace/project directory and make those MCP servers available for the current session, while clearly marking their source as project-provided config.

Possible behavior:

1. Hermes discovers a `.mcp.json` file in the current workspace/project directory.
2. Hermes reads MCP server definitions from that file and makes them available to the current Hermes session.
3. `hermes mcp list` shows both Hermes-configured MCP servers and project `.mcp.json` servers, with a clear source indicator, for example:
   - `config.yaml`
   - `.mcp.json`
4. If a server name exists in both Hermes config and `.mcp.json`, the explicit Hermes config entry should take precedence.
5. Project-local `.mcp.json` usage should be visible and/or opt-in, since MCP servers can run local commands.
6. Stdio MCP servers from `.mcp.json` should follow the same security/approval model as Hermes-native MCP servers.

Potential CLI options:

```bash
hermes mcp list --include-project
hermes mcp test --from-project unreal-mcp
hermes chat --use-project-mcp
hermes chat --mcp-from .mcp.json
```

Potential config option:

```yaml
mcp:
  use_project_mcp_json: true
```

The feature should support common .mcp.json shapes such as HTTP/SSE servers:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "unreal-mcp": {
      "url": "<http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp>"
    }
  }
}
```

and stdio servers:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-server": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "some-mcp-server"],
      "env": {
        "SOME_ENV": "value"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Optionally, Hermes could also provide an import command for users who want to copy a project `.mcp.json` server into Hermes' persistent config, but the main request is for Hermes to be able to use `.mcp.json` directly in-place as project/session MCP config.

### Alternatives Considered

The current workaround is to manually duplicate every MCP server into Hermes with commands like:

```bash
hermes mcp add unreal-mcp --url http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp
```

This works, but it creates two sources of truth: the project's `.mcp.json` and Hermes' own `config.yaml`.

Another workaround is to call an MCP HTTP endpoint directly with scripts, but that bypasses Hermes' native MCP tool discovery, tool selection, and normal UX.

The proposed solution is better because it lets Hermes participate in existing project-level MCP configuration while still preserving Hermes' own config model and security controls.

### Feature Type

New tool

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

```shell

```

items.title: Desktop: 'Delete API Key' only removes from .env, provider still appears in model list due to stale auth.json credentials
items.body:
## Bug Description

In the Hermes Desktop Settings page, when a user deletes an API key for a provider (e.g., Z.AI, MiniMax), only the key is removed from `~/.hermes/.env`. The registered credential in `~/.hermes/auth.json` is left intact, so the provider continues to appear in the model/provider selector dropdown — unusable (no key), but still visible.

This creates a confusing UX: the user expects "delete key" to remove the provider from the list entirely, but it doesn't.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop → Settings → find a provider with an API key (e.g., Z.AI / GLM, MiniMax)
2. Click "Delete Key" for that provider
3. Verify the key is gone from `~/.hermes/.env` ✓
4. Check `hermes auth list` → the credential entry for that provider is **still present** ✗
5. Go back to the model selector → the provider **still appears** in the dropdown ✗

## Expected Behavior

Option A (ideal): Deleting the key should also remove the corresponding credential from `auth.json`, making the provider disappear from the model list.

Option B (pragmatic): If the Desktop app cannot safely clean up `auth.json`, it should warn the user: "This provider still has a stored credential. Run `hermes auth remove <provider>` to fully remove it."

## Actual Behavior

The key is removed from `.env` only. Provider remains visible in the dropdown until manually cleaned via `hermes auth remove <provider>` in terminal.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop (macOS Tauri app)
- Hermes v0.17.0 / config v30
- macOS 26.5.1
- Active profile: default

## Additional Context

Affected at least two providers during testing: `zai` (Z.AI / GLM) and `minimax-cn` (MiniMax China). The root cause is the same in both cases — Desktop UI only manages `.env`, not `auth.json`.

Related: providers defined under `providers:` in `config.yaml` with embedded API keys are also invisible to the Desktop delete flow, but that's a separate (and rarer) edge case.

items.title: [Bug]: Honcho memory provider activates even when honcho-ai dependency is missing

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

When Hermes is configured with `memory_provider: honcho`, the memory provider appears to register and activate successfully, but the Honcho background session repeatedly fails because the `honcho-ai` Python package is missing from the running Hermes environment.

The confusing part is that Hermes logs both:
```
Memory provider 'honcho' registered (5 tools)
Memory provider 'honcho' activated
```
and then repeatedly logs:
```
Honcho background session init failed: honcho-ai is required for Honcho integration. Install it with: pip install honcho-ai  (or run hermes honcho setup to configure).
```

So from the user perspective Honcho looks enabled/active, but background Honcho functionality is not actually working.

In my environment this happened inside a Docker/Unraid Hermes gateway setup. Installing `honcho-ai` required extra manual work because the active Hermes venv was not writable from inside the running container.



### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable Honcho memory provider.
2. Start Hermes gateway.
3. Send any message through Discord.
4. Check `agent.log`.
5. Honcho is logged as activated, but background session init fails because `honcho-ai` is missing.

### Expected Behavior

When Honcho is configured as the memory provider, Hermes should either:

1. fully initialize Honcho successfully, including verifying that `honcho-ai` is installed in the runtime environment, or
2. clearly report that Honcho is unavailable/degraded because the required dependency is missing.

Hermes should not log `Memory provider 'honcho' activated` if Honcho background session initialization cannot actually run.

Ideally `hermes doctor`, `hermes config check`, or `hermes honcho setup` should catch this before runtime.

### Actual Behavior

Hermes reports the Honcho memory provider as registered and activated:

`Memory provider 'honcho' registered (5 tools)`
`Memory provider 'honcho' activated`

However, during the same gateway session, it repeatedly logs that Honcho background session initialization failed because the `honcho-ai` package is missing:

`Honcho background session init failed: honcho-ai is required for Honcho integration. Install it with: pip install honcho-ai  (or run hermes honcho setup to configure).`

This makes the runtime state ambiguous: Honcho appears to be active according to the main logs, but the background Honcho integration is failing. The warning repeats across turns/sessions instead of being surfaced once as a clear setup/configuration problem.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Discord
