items.title: GLM-5.x models return 429 from Zhipu z.ai while identical curl requests succeed

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes Agent consistently receives HTTP 429 rate-limit errors from the **Zhipu/z.ai API** on GLM-5.x models (glm-5, glm-5.1, glm-5.2), while **identical requests via curl, Python urllib, and other clients succeed** every time.

## Environment

- Hermes version: latest (updated 2026-06-22, 317 commits)
- Provider: `zai` (Zhipu AI) — `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`
- Model: `glm-5.2` (also fails on `glm-5` and `glm-5.1`)
- Platform: Linux (Debian)
- Session type: TUI

## What Works

| Client | Model | Tools | Stream | Result |
|--------|-------|-------|--------|--------|
| curl | glm-5.2 | 75 tools | true + stream_options | ✅ 200 |
| Python urllib | glm-5.2 | 75 tools | true + stream_options | ✅ 200 |
| Python urllib | glm-5.2 | 75 tools | false | ✅ 200 |
| OpenAI SDK (httpx) | glm-5.2 | 75 tools | — | ❌ 401 (auth header issue) |
| Hermes Agent | glm-5.2 | 75 tools | true | ❌ 429 |
| Hermes Agent | glm-4.7 | 75 tools | true | ✅ 200 |
| Hermes Agent | glm-5-turbo | 75 tools | true | ✅ 200 |

## What We Tested

1. **Replayed Hermes request dumps via curl** — exact same URL, headers, body structure (model, tools, stream_options) → 200 OK
2. **5 sequential curl requests** to glm-5.2 → 5/5 OK
3. **3 parallel curl requests** to glm-5.2 → 3/3 OK
4. **5 parallel curl requests** to glm-5.2 → 3/5 OK (2x 429, but recovers)
5. **Hermes new session, history=0, single message "proute"** → 429 on first call

## Key Observations

1. **Model-specific**: Only GLM-5.x models are affected. GLM-4.7 and GLM-5-turbo work fine through Hermes on the same provider/key.
2. **Not quota-related**: curl can make 5 sequential requests without any 429 on glm-5.2 using the same API key.
3. **Not request-related**: curl with identical payload (75 tools, stream, stream_options) returns 200.
4. **Eager fallback**: Hermes falls back immediately on first 429 when the credential pool has only 1 entry (`_pool_may_recover_from_rate_limit` returns `False` for single-entry pools). This is by design (conversation_loop.py line ~2794), but means Hermes never retries zai.
5. **Other Hermes profiles**: A separate profile (KM) also gets 429 on glm-5.2 but recovers via glm-5-turbo fallback on the same provider.
6. **bg-review threads**: Two bg-review threads ran overnight on the default profile, consuming 240K+ tokens each. These likely contributed to hitting rate limits, but the problem persists even on fresh sessions after they complete.
7. **429 pattern started**: Around 03:45 UTC on 2026-06-23. Before that, 240+ successful glm-5.2 calls on the same session.

## Possible Causes (Speculative)

- **TLS fingerprinting**: Hermes uses `httpx` (via OpenAI Python SDK). curl uses `libcurl`. They have different TLS fingerprints. Zhipu/z.ai might fingerprint and rate-limit `httpx` traffic differently for certain models.
- **Connection pooling / keep-alive**: Hermes may reuse HTTP connections that have accumulated rate-limit state, while curl creates fresh connections.
- **User-Agent or other implicit headers**: The OpenAI Python SDK may send headers (e.g., `User-Agent: OpenAI/Python/...`) that zai uses to identify and throttle agent traffic on specific models.

## Logs

```
09:59:31 conversation turn: model=glm-5.2 provider=zai history=0 msg='proute'
09:59:34 API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=RateLimitError: HTTP 429
09:59:34 Fallback activated: glm-5.2 → gemma4:31b (ollama-cloud)
```

Request dump available (redacted keys) if needed.

## Workaround

- Use `glm-5-turbo` or `glm-4.7` as primary model (both work through Hermes)
- Or set `glm-5-turbo` as first fallback on the `zai` provider (same provider, instant failover)

items.title: [Bug]: Title Generation sends main model name to fallback provider's endpoint

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

## Summary

When title generation falls back from the primary provider to the first `fallback_providers` entry, the resolved HTTP client correctly targets the fallback provider's base URL, but the **model name sent in the API request is the main session model** instead of the model configured for that fallback entry. Result: every title-generation call hits e.g. `https://api.deepseek.com` with `model: "MiniMax-M3"` and fails with HTTP 400.

## Environment

- **Component:** `hermes-agent` — title generation (`title_generator`)
- **Affected file:** `agent/auxiliary_client.py`
- **OS:** macOS 26.5.1
- **Config:**
  - `auxiliary.title_generation.provider` = `auto`
  - `auxiliary.title_generation.model` = empty (unset)
  - `fallback_providers[0]` = `{ provider: "deepseek", model: "deepseek-v4-flash" }`
- **Primary provider:** `minimax-oauth` (auth_type `oauth_minimax` is currently unhandled by `_resolve_*` — silent fail in Step 1)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the primary provider as `minimax-oauth` (or any provider whose `auth_type` is missing a branch in `resolve_provider_client`).
2. Configure `auxiliary.title_generation.provider: auto` (or leave unset) so resolution falls through to `fallback_providers`.
3. Ensure `fallback_providers` has at least one entry, e.g.:

   ```yaml
   fallback_providers:
     - provider: deepseek
       model: deepseek-v4-flash
   ```

4. Start a new session (any user message that triggers `title_generator.generate_title()`).
5. Observe the auxiliary log line and the API error.


### Expected Behavior

Title generation should send `model: "deepseek-v4-flash"` to the fallback provider's endpoint, e.g.:

```
Auxiliary title_generation: using auto (deepseek-v4-flash) at https://api.deepseek.com
→ 200 OK
```


### Actual Behavior

Log shows:

```
Auxiliary title_generation: using auto (MiniMax-M3) at https://api.deepseek.com
```

…and the request fails (HTTP 400, `Model Not Exist` / similar — exact error from provider).

The base URL is the fallback provider's, but the model name is the **main session model**.


### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/r7JuL
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/CQ9Yc
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/s0Iau
```

### Operating System

macOS Tahoe 26.5.1

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.17.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`agent/auxiliary_client.py`, in `resolve_provider_client` around lines **3564–3565** and **3630**:

```python
# ~line 3564-3565
if not model:
    model = _get_aux_model_for_provider(provider) or _read_main_model() or model
# → model is auto-filled with the main session model (e.g. "MiniMax-M3")

# ~line 3617-3630
if provider == "auto":
    client, resolved = _resolve_auto(main_runtime=main_runtime, task=task)
    # resolved = ("deepseek", "deepseek-v4-flash") from fallback chain

final_model = model or resolved
# → picks `model` (the auto-filled main model) over `resolved` (the correct fallback model)
```

When `provider == "auto"` and the caller passed `model=None`, the auto-fill path silently substitutes the **main** model name. `_resolve_auto` then correctly switches the **client / base URL** to the first fallback entry, but line 3630 prefers the caller-provided-or-auto-filled `model` over the `resolved` fallback model, so the wrong model name is sent to the fallback endpoint.

This is the classic "wrong model on the right endpoint" mismatch — base URL and model name come from different resolution paths and the priority logic is incorrect for the `auto` case.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

Either of these (in order of preference):

1. **Fix root cause** (preferred): in the `provider == "auto"` branch, after `_resolve_auto` returns `(client, resolved)`, prefer `resolved` when it is non-empty:

   ```python
   final_model = resolved if resolved else (model or _read_main_model())
   ```

   …and only fall back to `model` when `resolved` is None and `model` was explicitly passed by the caller (not auto-filled).

2. **Document / refuse auto-fill when `provider == "auto"`**: don't auto-substitute `_read_main_model()` for `model=None` inside `resolve_provider_client` when the caller is the auxiliary client; let the auto/fallback path own the model resolution entirely.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway child crashes (exit code 1) when cwd contains Python package named `utils`

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description

Starting Hermes TUI from a directory that contains a Python package named
`utils/` (or `proxy/`, `ui/` — any name that collides with Hermes internal
packages) causes the gateway child process to exit with code 1 immediately.
The TUI parent shows "gateway exited" repeatedly in a crash loop.

~/downloads/tg-ws-proxy/ — a Telegram WebSocket proxy project — has its own
utils/, proxy/, and ui/ packages in its repo root (it is also a venv).
Running Hermes from that directory triggers the bug.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a directory with a Python package named `utils`:
   mkdir -p /tmp/test-venv/utils
   touch /tmp/test-venv/utils/__init__.py

2. Run Hermes from that directory:
   cd /tmp/test-venv && hermes

3. Observe "gateway exited" crash loop.

Or reproduce the spawn directly:
   cd /tmp/test-venv && PYTHONPATH=/path/to/hermes-agent python3 -m tui_gateway.entry

### Expected Behavior

Hermes starts normally regardless of cwd contents.

### Actual Behavior

ImportError: cannot import name 'atomic_replace' from 'utils'
  (/tmp/test-venv/utils/__init__.py)

The gateway child exits with code 1. The TUI parent retries in a loop.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/jaaMO
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/GTYRz
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/qd1O4
```

### Operating System

Linux 6.10.6+bpo-amd64 (Debian Bookworm)

### Python Version

3.11.2

### Hermes Version

v0.17.0 (45bc4fb3)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Python always puts cwd (as empty string "") at sys.path[0], **before** any
PYTHONPATH entries. When cwd contains a `utils/` package, `from utils import
atomic_replace` in `hermes_cli/env_loader.py:10` finds the wrong `utils` first.

Chain: tui_gateway/server.py → hermes_cli/env_loader.py:10 →
  from utils import atomic_replace → picks up <cwd>/utils/__init__.py
  → ImportError → exit(1)

The spawn code in ui-tui/src/gatewayClient.ts sets PYTHONPATH but cannot
override cwd's priority in sys.path.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Option A — in tui_gateway/entry.py (before any imports):

  import sys, os
  sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

Option B — in ui-tui/src/gatewayClient.ts, prepend the Hermes root via a
wrapper script or -c flag that manipulates sys.path before -m tui_gateway.entry.

items.title: Feature Request: Add HERMES_TUI_WS_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S environment variable

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Summary

Add support for configuring the TUI Gateway WebSocket write timeout via environment variable `HERMES_TUI_WS_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S`.

## Problem

Currently, the WebSocket write timeout in TUI Gateway is hardcoded to 10 seconds in `tui_gateway/ws.py`:

```python
_WS_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S = 10.0
```

This causes connection drops when API calls take longer than 10 seconds, which is common with slower providers or large context windows.

## Impact

When using providers with variable latency (e.g., GLM, Claude with large contexts), the event loop can be blocked for 30-60+ seconds during API calls. This causes:

1. **WebSocket write timeouts** - `ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s)` warnings
2. **Connection drops** - Client disconnects unexpectedly
3. **Session loss** - Unsaved work and broken user experience

## Example Scenario

```
13:40:02 - API call started (session A)
13:40:51 - API call completed (latency: 68.7s)
13:42:00 - ws write slow warning (event loop still blocked from previous call)
13:44:08 - Final warning before connection drops
```

During this period, the TUI Gateway cannot write to WebSocket because the event loop is occupied handling the long-running API call.

## Proposed Solution

Add environment variable support similar to other TUI Gateway settings:

```python
# In tui_gateway/ws.py
_WS_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S = float(os.environ.get("HERMES_TUI_WS_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S", "10.0"))
```

This follows the same pattern as other HERMES_TUI_* environment variables:
- `HERMES_TUI_SLASH_TIMEOUT_S`
- `HERMES_TUI_WS_ORPHAN_REAP_GRACE_S`
- `HERMES_TUI_SESSION_TTL_S`
- `HERMES_TUI_RPC_POOL_WORKERS`

## Alternative Workaround

Users can reduce `max_concurrent_sessions` in config.yaml to lower the chance of concurrent API calls blocking the event loop, but this does not fully solve the problem when a single API call exceeds 10 seconds.

## Expected Behavior

With `HERMES_TUI_WS_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S=30`, the system would:
- Wait up to 30 seconds for WebSocket writes to complete
- Avoid premature connection drops during slow API calls
- Still properly detect and handle actual network failures

---

**Environment:**
- Hermes Agent version: latest
- Platform: Windows/macOS/Linux
- Provider: Custom (e.g., hc, GLM)

items.title: fix(delegate_task): silent timeout kills subagents without notifying parent session

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

`delegate_task` subagents that exceed the internal timeout (~5min) are silently killed. The `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE]` message is never delivered to the parent session. The parent session has no way to know the task failed — it appears as if the task is still running, and the user/agent waits indefinitely for a result that will never arrive.

## Reproduction

1. Dispatch a `delegate_task` with a research-heavy goal (e.g. 6+ `web_search` calls + content analysis)
2. The subagent runs for >5 minutes
3. The subagent is killed silently (no error, no completion message)
4. The parent session never receives `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE]`
5. The parent agent has no signal that the task failed — it may tell the user "the task is still running" or simply move on without reporting the failure

## Real-world impact

In a single session, 3+ research subagents were dispatched and all silently disappeared:
- Dark Factory orchestrator pattern research (6 web searches)
- Codex CLI token extraction research (web searches + terminal commands)
- Main-agent model choice research (5+ web searches)

Each ran for 6-10 minutes, exceeded the timeout, and was killed without any notification to the parent. The parent agent incorrectly reported "tasks are still running" to the user, who then asked "do they really still run?" — exposing the silent failure.

## Root cause

The `delegate_task` background execution has an internal timeout that kills long-running subagents. When the timeout fires:
1. The subagent process is terminated
2. No `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE]` (or equivalent timeout/error message) is delivered to the parent session
3. The parent session's context has no record that the delegation was attempted, timed out, or failed

This is distinct from:
- #48864 (gateway restart loses in-flight delegations) — our issue happens WITHOUT a restart
- #35986 (Kanban stale detection) — our issue is about delegate_task specifically, not Kanban

## Proposed fix

Three options, not mutually exclusive:

### Option A: Deliver timeout notification (minimal fix)
When a subagent times out, deliver a message to the parent session:
```
[ASYNC DELEGATION TIMEOUT — deleg_XXXX]
A background delegation has exceeded the timeout and was terminated.
Goal: <goal summary>
Duration: <elapsed>s
Partial output (if any): <last N lines>
```
This ensures the parent agent can react (retry, inform user, try alternative approach).

### Option B: Configurable timeout
Make the delegate_task timeout configurable:
- `delegate_task(goal=..., timeout=600)` — per-task timeout in seconds
- Or env var: `HERMES_DELEGATE_TASK_TIMEOUT=600`
- Default stays at current value (~300s) for backward compat
- Research-heavy tasks (web search, multi-step analysis) can opt into longer timeouts

### Option C: Heartbeat / progress signal
For long-running subagents, deliver periodic progress signals to the parent:
```
[ASYNC DELEGATION PROGRESS — deleg_XXXX]
Still running... 3/6 web searches completed, 180s elapsed
```
This gives the parent visibility without waiting for completion.

## Recommendation

**Option A + B together** would solve the immediate problem:
- A ensures no silent failure (the parent ALWAYS gets a message — success, error, or timeout)
- B allows research-heavy tasks to run longer without being killed

Option C is a nice-to-have for UX but not essential.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (by Nous Research)
- macOS 26.4.1
- Model: z-ai/glm-5.2 via OpenRouter
- delegate_task used extensively for cross-LLM research and validation tasks

Bug Report: Custom Providers Not Recognized by delegate_task Delegation System                                                  
                                                                                                                                    
    Summary                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                    
    The delegate_task tool and CLI --provider flag do not recognize custom providers defined in config.yaml, making it impossible   
    to use local LLMs (LM Studio, Ollama, etc.) for background tasks while keeping cloud models for the parent session.             
                                                                                                                                    
    Environment                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                    
    • Hermes Version: Latest (as of 2026-06-23)                                                                                     
    • OS: Linux (6.8.0-124-generic)                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                    
    Configuration                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                    
    Custom Provider Defined (Works for Parent Session)                                                                              
                                                                                                                                    
      ─ yaml                                                                                                                        
      providers:                                                                                                                    
        lms_studio:                                                                                                                 
          name: LMS Studio                                                                                                          
          type: custom                                                                                                              
          base_url: http://100.122.60.59:1234/v1                                                                                    
      model:                                                                                                                        
        default: kimi-k2.5                                                                                                          
        provider: ollama-cloud                                                                                                      
        lms_llama31:                                                                                                                
          id: llama-3.1-8b-instruct                                                                                                 
        default: kimi-k2.5                                                                                                          
        provider: ollama-cloud                                                                                                      
        lms_llama31:                                                                                                                
          id: llama-3.1-8b-instruct                                                                                                 
          provider: lms_studio                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                    
    Delegation Config (Does NOT Work)                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                    
      ─ yaml                                                                                                                        
      delegation:                                                                                                                   
        provider: lms_studio        # Custom provider - NOT recognized                                                              
        model: llama-3.1-8b-instruct                                                                                                
        base_url: http://100.122.60.59:1234/v1                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                    
    Expected Behavior                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                    
    delegate_task should use the provider specified in delegation.provider, including custom providers.

    1. Custom provider ignored — falls back to parent model (kimi-k2.5)                                                             
    2. CLI --provider lms_studio returns "Unknown provider"

    Support custom providers in delegation:

        provider: lms_studio        # Should resolve from providers: section
